Title: Statement to the International Monetary and Financial Committee on behalf of several countries
text: Algiers, 16 October 2011 ECONOMIC AND MONETARY DEVELOPMENTS IN 2010 AND TRENDS IN THE FIRST HALF OF 2011 1. International environment After more than two years of economic and financial crisis, the world economy returned to recovery in 2010. While the annual growth rate reached 5.1% (-0.7% in 2009), the strong pace was recorded mainly in the fourth quarter. However, the recovery of the world economy in 2010 was at different rates depending on the group of economies: strong growth in emerging and developing economies (7.3% compared to 2.8% in 2009) in the face of a still weak performance in advanced economies (3.1% against -3.7% in 2009). In the latter, the recovery remains fragile, given the severity of the recession. The return of economic growth in the euro area in 2010 (1.8%), to a slow pace after the severe recession of 2009 (-4.3%), in a context of high financial risks, was mainly based on the rebound in economic activity in Germany (3.6% against -5.1% in 2009) where domestic demand was strong. For the United States, after a weakness in economic activity in the second quarter of 2010, the growth rate in the third quarter exceeded the expected performance, followed by a rebound in the manufacturing production index and a solid spending index (retail sales and orders for capital goods), notably consumer spending, in the fourth quarter of 2010. The economic growth rate was 3% in 2010 (-3.5% in 2009), almost equal to that of advanced economies (3.1%). The strong recovery in the emerging economies of Asia (9.5% compared to 7.2% in 2009) and the performance of the Brazilian economy (7.5% against -0.6% in 2009) were the main drivers of the rapid recovery of emerging and developing economies, in the context of robust domestic demand and a strong rebound in international trade (12.8% against -10.7% in 2009). Economies in the MENA region recorded a growth of only 4.4% (2.6% in 2009) in the context of inflationary pressures, fuelling economic and social tensions in the context of high structural unemployment rates, mainly among young people. Sub-Saharan Africa performed better (5.4% in 2010 compared to 2.8% in 2009) than the MENA region. While the severe global economic crisis has led to historically high unemployment rates in advanced economies (8.3% in 2010), including 10.1% in the euro area and 9.6% in the United States, emerging asian economies, for their part, are facing inflationary pressures that seem to be combined with a risk of overheating linked to excessive credit expansion fuelled by large capital inflows of a relatively volatile nature. In these economies, both consumption and investment recovered strongly during 2010, against a backdrop of weak external demand. The surge in commodity prices in 2010, which quickly returned to their 2008 high levels, driven in particular by a structural factor represented by the continued rapid growth of emerging and developing economies despite the crisis, was combined with the return of inflationary expectations in China to their pre-crisis levels. Inflation is particularly high in India, with double-digit inflation at 12 per cent in 2010, and other developing countries in Asia (9.1 per cent in 2010), reflecting a certain dispersion of short-term inflationary expectations among emerging markets where food accounts for a high proportion of their consumption basket. The level of inflationary expectations is already high in these countries. In some Latin American countries (Venezuela, Argentina,...), inflation was very high in 2010. The recovery of the global economy in 2010, driven by strong growth in emerging and developing economies, continued in the first half of 2011, but at a slow pace. The fragility of the recovery increased in the second quarter with upside risks related to financial stability. Economic growth in many emerging and developing economies remained strong in the first half of 2011, particularly in China and India, but also in Sub-Saharan Africa and, to a lesser extent, in Latin America. Conversely, the economic performance of advanced economies weakened in the second quarter and unemployment rates remained high. Serious vulnerabilities in some of these countries, including weak public finances and the financial sector, weighed on the pace of recovery in the first half of the year. The sovereign debt crisis in some eurozone countries, the rise in commodities and energy products, recent disasters in Japan and developments in some countries in the Middle East and North Africa have heightened uncertainties. At the global level, financial volatility has picked up sharply and tensions in interbank markets have increased, fuelled by the sovereign debt crisis at the euro area level and by weak activity in advanced economies in the second quarter of 2011 despite the continuation of stimulative monetary policies in the United States and the euro area, notably through various quantitative easing programs. Monetary conditions thus remain very accommodative, despite the recovery in inflation in both the United States and the euro area; however, core inflation remains low. In contrast, several emerging-market central banks have taken monetary tightening measures to contain strong credit growth. However, it remains high, fuelled by large capital flows to these countries, and interest rates remain below their pre-international financial crisis level. The volatile nature of capital inflows, in the context of inflationary pressures recorded in the first half of 2011, is increasing financial vulnerability in some emerging countries. 2. Economic and financial developments in 2010 After the effect of the large external shock of 2009 inherent in the international financial crisis and the global economic crisis, the national economy achieved significant financial performance in 2010, including a consolidation of the net external financial position. 2.1. Backed by the sustained recovery in the price of a barrel of oil in 2010 (80.15 compared to 62.26 in 2009) and correspondingly to the sharp increase in hydrocarbon export earnings (26.4%), the current account balance recorded a significant surplus in 2010 (12.16 billion, 7.5% of GDP), in a situation of slight increase in imports (4%) where the relative share of capital goods and semi-finished products is close to two-thirds. This performance in the external current account benefited from the slight decline in the services deficit, the near equilibrium of the item (net) factor income in the context of appreciable income from the investment of foreign exchange reserves and the stabilization of the surplus of the current transfers (net). This confirmed the excess of saving over investment that characterized the 2000s, with the exception of 2009. After the external current account deficit in the first half of 2009, the surplus in 2010 is all the more appreciable as the balance of the current account balance becomes the central element of Algeria's external balance of payments situation. The capital account, which, after the external deleveraging completed before the international financial crisis, is mainly limited to foreign direct investment (net), is also in surplus (3.4 billion). In particular, the latter improved in 2010 (3.5 billion compared to 2.5 billion in 2009), following a net outflow of capital from foreign direct investment in certain sectors. As a result, the marked improvement in the overall external balance of payments surplus in 2010 (15.58 billion compared to 3.86 billion in 2009) fuelled Algeria's level of official foreign exchange reserves, which exceed three years (38.33 months) of imports of goods and services. The level of official foreign exchange reserves (including SDR holdings) stood at 162.22 billion at the end of 2010 (148.9 billion at the end of 2009), while medium- and long-term external debt stabilized (3.679 billion) and now represents only 2.27 percent of the estimated gross domestic product for 2010. These main parameters of Algeria's net external financial position confirm its solidity and strengthen its resilience to external shocks, especially since the Bank of Algeria's exchange rate management policy effectively contributes to external financial stability. In 2010, the intervention of the Bank of Algeria in the interbank foreign exchange market resulted in the appreciation of the real effective exchange rate of the dinar on an annual average (2.64%). The real effective exchange rate of the dinar remained almost at equilibrium in the medium term, despite the increased volatility of the exchange rates of the main currencies and the structural weakness of non-hydrocarbon exports (about one billion dollars in 2010). The structure of external payments indicates that the share of payments in euros stabilizes at 46% against 50% for the dollar; the structure of foreign trade with Algeria's fifteen main trading partners serving as the basis for weighting the real effective exchange rate and the basket of reference currencies. In this context, the level of official foreign exchange reserves is of particular importance as it is the main bulwark against possible external shocks. Thus, external financial stability in the medium and long term is strongly based on the continued prudent management of official foreign exchange reserves by the Bank of Algeria. The objectives pursued in this area are to: Preserve the value of capital: minimize the risk of loss of the market value of assets, maintaining a diversified portfolio of high-quality assets (in credit rating term and issuer type) and applying appropriate risk mitigation practices; Maintain a high level of liquidity: place reserves in assets that mature or can be resold quickly without loss of value; Optimize returns: achieve the best possible return while respecting security and liquidity objectives. As a result, while deposits have been made particularly with central banks and supranational financial institutions since 2007, securities portfolios, whose share has since increased to an average of 98% of total reserves, are invested in best-rated and therefore least risky instruments, mainly sovereign bonds. In terms of returns, the Investments made by the Bank of Algeria in securities portfolios during the years when interest rates were high continue to generate relatively high returns, at nearly 3% in 2010 and above 3% in 2008 and 2009. These performances are all the more appreciable as they are achieved in the context of very low interest rates in advanced countries and key rates close to zero, particularly in the United States. In addition, it is important to stress that real rates of return remain positive. The diversification initiated since 2004, both in terms of the choice of currencies used in the composition of reserves and their distribution at the portfolio level, and in terms of securities, by risk class, has contributed to this performance, while minimizing risks. The objective of security remains paramount, especially since the international environment was marked in 2010 by the emergence of sovereign debt risks in a context of rising banking risks. 2.2. While the average annual inflation differential between Algeria and the euro area has narrowed, while still remaining high, the appreciation of the real effective exchange rate of the dinar has helped to limit the impact of imported inflation on the general price level, especially since the prices of consumer goods with a high import content recorded a strong increase in 2010 (7%). The increase in international prices of imported agricultural commodities (cereals and tropical products), the increase in the money supply and the increase in the wholesale prices of fresh fruit and vegetables are the main factors that explain and determine inflation, with contributions estimated at 31%, 62% and 7% respectively on average over the decade. It is important here to highlight the inflationary impact of the dysfunctions of the internal markets. For the first time in five years, the average annual inflation rate as measured by the consumer price index fell from 6.1% in 2009 to 4.1% for the national index and from 5.7% in 2009 to 3.9% for the Greater Algiers index. In contrast to previous years, inflation in 2010 is mainly driven by higher prices for services and manufactured goods, although food goods have experienced substantial increases, which are significantly lower than in the past. If since 2003, the rise in consumer prices has been lower in Algeria than in the MENA region and lower than the median inflation for all these years, the slowdown in the growth rate of industrial producer prices since 2008 and consumer prices in 2010 suggests that a disinflation dynamic is underway in Algeria, this dynamic must be reinforced by controlling the main determinants of inflation: non-hydrocarbon money creation in line with real growth, controlling rising factor costs and stimulating supply. 2.3. Thus, after two years of moderate economic activity at 2.4 %, the recovery in growth, driven by domestic demand, itself supported by the increase in resources, was confirmed in 2010 (3.3 %), while the hydrocarbon sector recorded negative growth since 2006. Indeed, all sectors of activity other than hydrocarbons experienced positive growth, with a weak performance of industry (0.9% against 5% in 2009) and agriculture (6.0% against 20.0% in 2009); non-hydrocarbon GDP in volume terms grew by 6.0% in 2010 (9.3% in 2009). The appreciable growth excluding hydrocarbons, unevenly distributed by sector, is driven by the increase in the contribution of the market services sectors, in particular trade and transport, non-market and construction, in the context of a decline in manufacturing and agriculture. At the same time, growth in domestic expenditure has slowed, but remains high at 5.5% in volume terms in 2010, driven by strong growth in household and general government spending, confirming the role of public spending as a decisive stimulus for economic activity in Algeria. While total budgetary expenditure increased by 6.3% in 2010, after its quasi-stabilisation in 2009, capital expenditure fell in both 2009 and 2010 by 1.4% and 6% respectively, after its strong increase since 2005. Their growth rate peaked at 41.3 per cent in 2007 (37.5 per cent in 2008). Also, after many years of upward developments, the ratio of capital expenditure to GDP fell from 19.4% in 2009 to 15.1% in 2010, reflecting the significant slowdown in capital absorption. The ratio of current expenditure to GDP stabilised in 2010 (22.3% compared with 22.9% in 2009), while the increase in current expenditure resulted in particular from that of staff costs. In addition, the coverage rate of operating expenditures by non-hydrocarbon revenues remained stable in 2010 (54.8%), following a decrease from 2006 to 2008. In 2010, hydrocarbon revenues increased by 20.4% to 66.3% of total budgetary revenues and covering 64.4% of total budgetary expenditures. Non-hydrocarbon revenues, representing 33.6 per cent of total budget revenues, increased by 16.5 per cent (14.6 per cent in 2009), while the relative share of tax revenues was 87.6 per cent. Moreover, while the ratio of non-hydrocarbon revenues to non-hydrocarbon gross domestic product remained stable in 2010 (18.7%), this stability should not overshadow the change in the structure of non-hydrocarbon taxation during the years 2004-2010. Indeed, levies on corporate income, wages and profits have increased relatively faster than levies on economic activity (taxes on goods and services and customs duties), despite the substantial increase in the latter's base. In total, after nearly a decade of surpluses, the overall balance of Treasury operations is in deficit for the second consecutive year (0.9% of GDP in 2010 and 7.1% in 2009). Despite this deficit, the Treasury's financing capacity consolidated in 2010, judging by the outstanding resources of the revenue regulation fund, which increased by 526.4 billion dinars to 40.2% of gross domestic product. This strengthens the sustainability of public finances, despite the increase in domestic public debt in 2010. The effectiveness of public investment must now be the ultimate goal. Particular attention should be paid to the continued strengthening of investment capacities. 2.4. The resumption in 2010 of the increase in accumulated resources (financial savings) in the Revenue Regulation Fund, despite the strong increase in current budgetary expenditure (staff costs and transfers) compared to its evolution in 2009, has helped to mitigate monetisation. The analysis of the sources of money creation in 2010 confirms that external assets (in foreign currency) constitute the essential element in this process and therefore in the formation of the financial savings of non-financial economic agents. Thus, the outstanding net foreign assets of the Bank of Algeria expressed in dinars, i.e. 11854.02 billion at the end of 2010, was monetized at 72.4% (excluding valuation). Given the weakness of banks' net foreign assets, the additional money creation is represented by loans to the economy (3671.1 billion dinars) distributed by banks and financial institutions. As a result, all these assets, consisting mainly of external assets (foreign exchange reserves), are matched by the stock of financial savings (deposits in banks and fiat money) of enterprises. and households (8323.28 billion dinars at the end of 2010) and the outstanding financial savings (revenue regulation fund and other deposits in current accounts at the Bank of Algeria and banks) of the State (5108.13 billion dinars at the end of 2010). It is in such a context of development of financial savings that the combined effect of sterilization by the Treasury and the absorption of excess liquidity by the Bank of Algeria contributed to further anchoring monetary and financial stability in 2010, despite the resumption of the expansion of the M2 money supply (13.8%) and the persistence of strong growth in fiat money (14.7% against 18.8% in 2009). The latter phenomenon is characteristic of the monetary behaviour of households and businesses and therefore their increased preference for cash, despite the modernisation of payment systems. After a historically low monetary expansion recorded in 2009 (3.1%) as a result of the large external shock, 2010 was marked by a return to monetary expansion (13.8%), but at a rate lower than the high rates of the years 2006 to 2008. With an increase of 10.2% in 2010, the resumption of the role of net foreign assets in the money creation process was combined with the continued dynamism of credit to the economy. Contrary to the situation in several emerging countries that have recorded a contraction in credit to the economy linked to the international financial crisis, loans distributed by banks operating in Algeria to companies and households, directly or through investment in bonds issued by companies, increased by 15.6% in 2010 (excluding the purchase of non-performing loans by the Treasury). This increase corresponds to a strong growth in loans, in real terms, during 2010, placing Algeria in the group of emerging countries with rapid credit growth. As a result of the strong growth in medium- and long-term loans, the share of these loans rose to 59.9% at the end of 2010 compared to 57.2% at the end of 2009, confirming the long-term financing momentum of investment projects, particularly in bank syndication, and thus contributing to the extension of bank financing maturities. In Algeria, favourable financial conditions and the resilience of the banking system in the face of the external shock have helped to strengthen the role of the credit channel in the allocation of savings resources; these consolidated during 2010, both in the hydrocarbon sector and in other sectors of activity, after the contraction of deposits in the hydrocarbon sector in 2009. It is worth noting that at the end of 2010, the outstanding financial savings of private households and enterprises exceeded that of public enterprises, including hydrocarbons. As a result, the substantial increase in bank deposits (sight and term in dinars) in 2010, 12.5% compared to a decrease of 8.2% in 2009, helped to further consolidate the banks' lending fund capacity, anchored on stable and increased resources and a good liquidity position. In addition, excess liquidity is increasingly scattered at the level of the banks of the place. This has, however, led to less dynamic activity in the interbank money market. Indeed, having stable financial resources enabling them to carry out their various activities in a context of low liquidity risk, banks have only rarely intervened on the money market to obtain liquidity during 2010, in particular to meet the objectives of setting up regulatory minimum reserves. Despite the acuteness of the excess structural liquidity fuelled by the significant recovery in monetary growth in 2010, the orderly conduct of monetary policy by the Bank of Algeria helped to contain inflationary pressures in 2010 and thus further establish monetary stability. The effective conduct of monetary policy has been based on the effective absorption of excess liquidity, given the magnitude of the monetization of external assets, which increased significantly in 2010 after the external shock of 2009. In addition, if free reserves constituted on average an amount of 63 billion dinars in 2010, it is important to note that of this amount, the free deposits of banks, which do not intervene in operations with the Bank of Algeria, reach 54 billion dinars. 3. Reform of the monetary policy framework in 2010 and financial stability Following an adjustment in 2009 of the regulatory framework for monetary policy instruments (liquidity recovery, interest-bearing deposit facility and minimum reserves), drawing lessons from the severe international financial crisis of 2008, 2010 was marked by the reform of the monetary policy framework where the inflation target was established as the ultimate objective of monetary policy, while maintaining quantitative monetary targets. The inflation target thus becomes decisive in relation to the current flexible quantitative monetary targeting, knowing that the forecast of inflation in the short term now takes on particular importance. Before the introduction of the inflation target, inflation forecasting and its monitoring led the Bank of Algeria to develop an appropriate tool since September 2009, namely a short-term inflation forecasting model responding to the concern for a forward-looking vision, in order to forecast the inflation rate and its evolution over a monthly horizon of one year. For example, the forecast of annual average inflation for the end of 2010 made in September 2010 differs only 0.14 percentage points from the inflation rate achieved and calculated by the ONS for December (3.91%). Accordingly average annual inflation remained close to short-term forecasts. This inflation rate is down compared to the rise in prices at the end of 2009 (5.74%) and in line with the inflation target set by the Currency and Credit Council (4%, or - 1 point) for the year 2010, as the implicit objective of monetary policy. The contribution of monetary policy to financial stability remains decisive in Algeria, given the predominance of banks in the Algerian financial system. This contribution is reinforced, in a situation of flexible exchange rate management in line with the objective of external financial stability. Similarly, the prudent management of official foreign exchange reserves, at a level that can cope with potential external shocks, is part of the strategic objective of consolidating financial stability. The new legislative provisions (Ordinance No. 10-04 of 26 August 2010) consolidate the legal framework governing the banking sector in Algeria and strengthen the legal anchoring of financial stability as an explicit mission of the Bank of Algeria, particularly from the perspective of the supervision of systemic risk. This reinforces the regulatory measures taken in recent years, in particular Regulation No. 08-04 of December 2008 which substantially increased the minimum capital of banks and financial institutions and Regulation No. 09-03 of May 2009 laying down general rules on banking conditions relating to risks on financial products, in the light of certain vulnerabilities identified. The Bank of Algeria now has broader prerogatives to launch any investigation at the level of banks and financial institutions, especially since the inspectors of the Bank of Algeria have the mission of conducting any control at the level of these institutions, particularly on behalf of the Banking Commission. The strengthening of the prerogatives of the Central Bank allows a greater capacity for early detection of vulnerabilities, through better monitoring of banks and financial institutions. In this context, the Bank of Algeria has consolidated its stress testing capabilities, in parallel with the finalization of the new rating system for banks and financial institutions, from the perspective of better control of banking risks (risk-based supervision). The Financial Stability Committee of the Bank of Algeria, for its part, reviews the financial soundness indicators for the 11 indicators called "minimum indicators", with a view to taking into account the other indicators called "proposed indicators". The periodic assessment of the stability of the banking and financial system, including through stress tests that have been developed since 2007, received particular attention in 2010. With regard to macroprudential instruments (minimum reserves, etc.), the Financial Stability Committee focused more in 2010 on excess liquidity. structural structure that characterizes the Algerian banking system, after the external shock of 2009. It is in this context that the need to improve the distribution of credit to the economy in support of the diversification of the national economy emerges, bearing in mind that credit risk remains the main banking risk. Hence the continuation of the objective of reducing the risks associated with non-performing loans in 2010 (19% compared to 21.8% in 2009). Finally, the new legislative provisions of August 2010 significantly strengthened the "crisis" prevention and resolution system, with particular emphasis on the risk orientation of banking supervision. The intensification of the exchange of information between the various supervisory authorities of the financial sector (Bank of Algeria, Banking Commission, Treasury, Insurance Supervisory Authority and COSOB), aimed at refining and strengthening knowledge of the level of resilience of the financial system in the face of business cycles, makes it possible to detect any threat to financial stability. A stress test of the financial system, by institution and as a whole, to internal and external financial shocks was carried out in May 2010, with the support of experts from the World Bank. This is a "stress testing" exercise that has made it possible to test, in particular, the level of information sharing between the various supervisory authorities of the financial system and their coordination in terms of taking corrective actions. 4. Strengthening banking supervision in 2010 The year 2010 is marked by the strengthening of the institutional framework of banking supervision following the new provisions introduced by Ordinance No. 10-04 of 26 August 2010, amending and supplementing Ordinance No. 03-11, relating to money and credit. This ordinance gives a legal anchor to financial stability, as the mission of the Bank of Algeria after that of price stability, and provides for new legal provisions aimed at better risk control by banks and financial institutions. As part of its action plan for the 2010 financial year, the General Directorate of the General Inspectorate (DGIG) of the Bank of Algeria has intensified its on-the-spot inspection interventions with banks and financial institutions in the area. The year under review was marked by the initiation of a simultaneous mission, conducted with all the banks of the place as well as the financial services of Algeria Post, evaluating their internal measures to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism. This mission took place as part of the actions undertaken by the public authorities in the fight against economic scourges (money laundering, etc.). Despite the mobilization of most of the staff of the inspectors of the Bank of Algeria for the realization of this operation, namely twenty-three (23) missions carried out in 2010 as part of the control of the anti-money laundering system with the banks and financial services of Algeria Post, other missions on various themes were also carried out during the 2010 financial year, covering in particular the areas of full control, valuation of the credit portfolio, foreign trade operations, and special investigations relating to the banking operations of bank customers. In addition, particular attention has been paid to the full monitoring and evaluation of the credit portfolio of banks, both public and private. Also, of the ten (10) full control missions carried out in 2010, some of which were continued in the first half of 2011, five (05) were the subject of inspection reports transmitted, in accordance with the procedures in force, to the Banking Commission. In addition, three (03) specific foreign trade control missions were carried out in 2010 and concerned operations carried out by foreign-invested companies. Foreign trade control work has in some cases led to reports of foreign exchange offences. In order to ensure a convergence of supervisory actions with the fundamental principles of effective banking supervision, laid down by the Basel Committee, the Bank of Algeria continued in 2010 the project to modernize the risk-based supervision function. This action is part of the strengthening of preventive actions to further promote the stability of the banking system in Algeria. This structuring project, whose effective implementation at the level of banks is scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2011 as a pilot phase, advocates a redesign of all the processes related to the control activities carried out by the General Directorate of the General Inspection of the Bank of Algeria. It includes the development of a bank rating system in accordance with international standards. This new system aims to strengthen the capacity for detection and early warning and to promote the predictive approach to control. The detection of early signs of failure by troubled banks and financial institutions is essential to ensure the stability of the financial system and the protection of depositors. It allows for a rapid reaction by the supervisory authority and the taking of adequate corrective measures to deal with the difficulties encountered by a financial institution. This new risk-forecasting approach will enable supervisory bodies to significantly reduce the cost of supervision by promoting a better understanding of the risk profile of each financial institution audited, a targeting of those in difficulty and a rational use of supervisory resources. This will quickly discriminate against healthy financial institutions from those in difficulty. 5. Indicators of financial soundness of the banking sector in 2010 At the end of 2010, the banking system in Algeria consists of twenty (20) universal banks, including six (6) public and fourteen (14) private with foreign capital, subsidiaries or branches of international banks, and six (6) financial institutions. In terms of the evolution of their uses and resources, the activity of both public and private banks remained dynamic, judging by the growth in their total assets (including accruals and deferred income). The total assets of public banks increased from 6497 billion dinars at the end of 2009 to 7067 billion dinars at the end of 2010, an increase of 8.8% against 11.3% for private banks. The growth in the assets of public and private banks is marked by the increase in credit activity, indicating a predominance of the traditional profession. Indeed, in 2010, the growth of loans to business and household customers reached 15.6% while bank deposits recorded a growth of 11.7%. As a large proportion of deposits consist of demand deposits that do not generate interest charges for banks, this situation has a positive impact on their income statements. In such a context of low cost of resources and increased credits, public banks made profits of around 71.860 billion dinars in 2010 (after deduction of provisions of reserves that are part of equity) against 70.229 billion dinars in 2009 while private banks saw their profits increase substantially in 2010 (24,158 million dinars against 15,614 million dinars in 2009). This financial performance of banks strengthens the resilience of the banking system, judging also by the relevant indicators of financial soundness used at the international level. In terms of solvency ratios, banks have raised the level of their own funds, including core capital, which is the most effective protection for depositors against unexpected losses. Indeed, both public and private banks have capital levels well above the regulatory minimum. The capital adequacy ratio to the risks involved (solvency ratio) increased from 22.11% in 2009 to 23.31% in 2010, while common equity constitutes a large proportion of it with an adequacy ratio increasing from 17.33% in 2009 to 18.76% in 2010. This performance is due to the allocation of a large part of the results of previous years to reserves and significant results of the year under review for public and private banks. At the level of public banks, regulatory and core capital increased by 12.81% and 17.49% respectively to 570.936 billion dinars and 422.196 billion dinars at the end of 2010. Private banks, for their part, recorded a smaller increase than public banks because of the much larger distribution of dividends. Their regulatory equity increased by 10.79% (10.90% for core equity) reaching levels of 198.653 billion dinars and 197.289 billion dinars respectively. Public and private banks continued their sustained efforts to rebuild capital, enabling them to improve the ratio of non-performing loans (net of accrued provisions) to regulatory capital from 30.04% in 2009 to 20.37% in 2010. In terms of the quality of banks' portfolios, banks continued to improve their credit risk management and the dynamic treatment of classified claims. This resulted in a slight improvement in the gross depreciation rate of the credit portfolio to 19.05% in 2010 from 21.82% in 2009. In terms of provisioning, their level reached 74.14% at the end of 2010 against 68.29% at the end of 2009. However, the proportion of non-performing loans remains high compared to international standards in this area. The profitability of the banking system is satisfactory and remains favourable for both public and private banks. That of private banks was materialized by an increase in almost all interim management balances following the positive evolution of their intermediation and non-intermediation activities. The increase in the return on their assets was 3.49% in 2010 compared to 3.28% in 2009. For public banks, the return on assets fell slightly to 1.25% in 2010 from 1.33% in 2009, due to the importance of their operations with the Bank of Algeria, which are less well remunerated. As for the return on capital of banks, it has decreased for both public and private banks, due to the substantial increase in their capital (capital plus reserves). As for the interest margin/gross income ratio, it improved in 2010 for both public and private banks as a result of the increase in net interest margins. While private banks are increasing their dependence on non-interest income, this is used to offset the decline in their intermediation margin, judging by the decrease in the ratio of non-interest charges to gross income from 52.73% in 2009 to 39.24% in 2010. Banks' liquidity position is strong. Measured by one of the standard indicators, the liquidity of banks is high, as evidenced by the absence of interbank debt and the increased intervention of the Bank of Algeria to absorb in a way effective excess liquidity on the money market. This reflects banks' ability to repay their short-term liabilities with liquid assets. Finally, it is clear from the analysis of the financial soundness indicators that public and private banks, despite the differences noted, recorded a significant improvement in their results (including reserve provisions) during the 2010 financial year, thanks in particular to the reduction in credit risk charges, the reduction of asset impairments and the control of operating expenses. The banking sector is, on the whole, strong and resilient. 6. Key monetary and financial trends in the first half of 2011 In the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), global uncertainties and recent events in the region are having a negative impact on economic activity and the financial situation in some countries, in particular due to the contraction of tourism receipts, remittances of workers abroad, capital and investment flows that have contributed to the slowdown in economic activity and the rise in unemployment, while inflationary pressures, inherent in rising world food and energy prices, have increased. As far as Algeria is concerned, the large budgetary savings and the substantial increase in foreign exchange reserves, linked to the high level of oil prices, offer considerable room for manoeuvre. Also, Algeria, while continuing to expand capital (investment) spending, has had to resort to increasing current fiscal spending to support domestic demand and mitigate the erosion of the purchasing power of households, especially the poorest. The budgetary measures taken since the first quarter of 2011 consisted mainly of increasing subsidies for food prices and social transfers, particularly to the unemployed, suspending taxes on certain basic products, raising wages, increasing employment in the civil service, particularly non-permanent jobs, and subsidizing housing financing. The sharp increase in current expenditure is mainly due to the increase in personnel costs and current transfers. This last item amounted to 1150.3 billion dinars in the first half of the current year, disbursed mainly in the second quarter, and up 70.3% compared to their amount in the first half of 2010 (675.6 billion dinars). In particular, subsidies to LFAs are rising sharply as well as the various other supports taken. in charge by the budget, testifying to the increased effort of the State in terms of social coverage in 2011. As a result, the coverage rate of operating expenses by non-hydrocarbon revenues stood at 42.1% in the first half of 2011 compared to 54.8% in 2010, in a context of increased importance of budgetary revenues from hydrocarbons. The favourable development of hydrocarbon prices in the first half of 2011 is also reflected in the appreciable surplus in the external current account, which is a better level compared to last year's half-year performance. Non-hydrocarbon exports, despite their structural weakness, increased in the first half of 2011, reaching their 2009 level (0.77 billion) compared to 0.53 billion in the first half of 2010. On a half-year basis, the overall increase recorded was nearly 46%. Imports of goods (fob) increased by 15.7%, mainly due to higher imports of food and consumer goods, reaching 22.37 billion in the first half of 2011 compared to 19.33 billion in the same period last year. This increase was particularly in food products (60.7%). For example, imports (cif) of the three main food products (cereals, milk and sugar) amounted to 3.44 billion in the first half of 2011, almost the value of annual imports in 2010 (3.66 billion); cereals accounting for 59.4% of these imports. While this increase in imports of basic foodstuffs responds to the concern for increased availability of these products on the domestic market, it is due in particular to a strong price effect inherent in imports of food and consumer goods. As for all imports, they recorded a contraction in volume of almost 9% compared to the first half of 2010. With regard to the capital account, in the first half of 2011 it recorded an increase in FDI capital inflows, which are estimated at 1.331 billion, in a situation of significant repayments of external debt, particularly short-term debt. The latter's outstanding assets increased from 1.778 billion at the end of December 2010 to 0.989 billion at the end of June 2011. In total, the overall balance of payments balance for the first half of 2011 reached 9.11 billion, or more than 4 billion on a quarterly basis. Algeria's external financial position has thus consolidated, in a situation of declining external debt and sustained accumulation of foreign exchange reserves (173.9 billion). at the end of June 2011, excluding SDR and gold assets). Flexible exchange rate management has resulted in the dinar's real effective exchange rate remaining almost at equilibrium in the medium term, despite increased volatility in the exchange rates of the main currencies. In addition, the first half of 2011 was marked by a narrowing of the inflation differential between Algeria and its main trading partners. Indicators of the monetary situation at the end of June 2011 show a relatively large increase in the money supply (8.62%), mainly through the monetization of external assets, as well as an overall significant increase in loans to the economy (11.16%). This trend confirms the continued dynamism of credit to the economy and places Algeria in the group of emerging countries with rapid credit growth. In addition, the increase in loans (excluding bonds) concerns both public banks (11.29%) and private banks (16.44%), while its pace is uneven between banks. However, from a sectoral perspective, the evolution of loans distributed by banks is mixed in the first half of 2011, as the appreciable increase in credit to private companies (10.21%) was accompanied by a larger increase in loans to the public sector (13.48%) and a moderate increase in loans to households (3.47%). Nevertheless, mortgages to households increased by 12.50% and reached 74% of total loans to households (68% at the end of 2010). The share of loans to the private sector (private enterprises and households) in total loans distributed net of redemptions stabilized in the first half of the year (55.18%). At the same time, the share of short-term loans is declining in favour of medium- and long-term loans, which reached 62.57% compared to 59.89% at the end of December 2010. The dynamism of medium- and long-term financing of investment projects, particularly in bank syndication, is thus reinforced and supported by an extension of bank financing maturities. The latter phenomenon will become more apparent in the second half of 2011, as a result of the impetus provided by the public authorities (financial support). In addition, in a context of strong growth in loans to the economy, the weighted average interest rate by type of credit decreased slightly in the first half of the year compared to its level at the end of 2010 and the end of 2009. Thus, favourable financial conditions and enhanced financial strength of banks contribute to strengthening the role of the credit channel in the allocation of increased financial savings resources in 2011, whether deposits of private households and companies or public enterprises, including hydrocarbons. For the first six months of 2011, demand deposits in banks increased by 6.55%, a slower pace than term deposits (including foreign currency deposits) (7.22%), while deposits in the CCP and the Treasury recorded a much larger increase (21.84%). It is also important to note a significant increase in fiat money from 2007 onwards, at an average annual rate of 18.2% over the last four years, whose ratio to the money supply reached 26.09% at the end of June 2011. While this ratio was relatively stable between 2005 and 2008, at around 22%, the surge in fiat money in circulation is mainly due to the increased scale of cash payments of transactions, beyond those in retail trade. At the end of June 2011, the money supply (excluding deposits in the hydrocarbon sector) increased by 10.67% compared to 8.62% for the broader M2 aggregate, since deposits in the hydrocarbon sector recorded a contraction of 6.29% compared to December 2010; the latter being linked to the payment of oil taxation in June 2011. Faced with the contraction of deposits in the hydrocarbon sector at the end of June 2011 compared to the end of December 2010, demand and term deposits in dinars of private companies and households at the level of banks consolidated more in the first half of 2011 (8.32%). In a situation of stabilization of their foreign currency deposits, the increased importance of household dinar deposits is fueled by the increase in wage incomes and budgetary transfers. It is important to note that household dinar deposits reached 36.57% of all dinar deposits at the end of June 2011 and are stable. Also, the significant increase in the financial assets of "non-hydrocarbon companies and households" agents has fuelled the excess liquidity of banks, which has remained structural and, moreover, scattered at the level of banks. For its part, the Bank of Algeria continued to absorb excess liquidity through seven-day and three-month recovery operations, while banks regularly placed the amounts in addition to the minimum reserve requirement target as a 24-hour remunerated deposit facility. As a result, the amount of free reserves contracted in the first half of 2011, reflecting the effective nature of the absorption of excess liquidity by the Bank of Algeria. In addition, in the first half of 2011, banks consolidated their financial strength indicators. Indeed, the solvency ratio remains appreciable at nearly 21%, while both liquidity ratios are high as at the end of 2010. In addition, it is important to note that the level of non-performing loans reported by banks is down from 19.05% of total loans distributed at the end of 2010 to 16.63% at the end of June 2011. This improvement is due to the combined effect of the decrease in the level of non-performing loans and the increase in the stock of loans distributed. To further develop the operational framework for financial stability and in line with the new Basel Committee standards, regulations on the identification, measurement, management and control of liquidity risk were issued by the Currency and Credit Council in May 2011. In addition, this regulation establishes a minimum liquidity ratio that banks and financial institutions must comply with at all times. The assessment made by the Bank of Algeria in June 2011 indicates that the banks of the place meet this requirement; this year is characterized by a broader and widely dispersed bank liquidity. Also, in order to establish a better practice of liquidity management and monitoring of interbank operations and to improve the quality of prudential reporting, the Currency and Credit Council also issued in May 2011 a second regulation establishing a system of internal supervision and counterparty limitation of outstanding interbank loans and borrowings, in particular those operated on the money market, which banks and financial institutions are required to set up. These two new mechanisms, which strengthen the instruments of supervision and control, contribute to further strengthening the stability and soundness of the Algerian banking system. They de facto consolidate the operational framework for forecasting and monitoring bank liquidity by the Bank of Algeria as part of its conduct of monetary policy. Inflation monitoring and control is now at the forefront of inflation, pursuant to new legislation on money and credit (August 2010). In the first half of 2011, the upward trend in the pace of monetary expansion combined with the rise in the prices of imported agricultural products amplified domestic price inflation. In the first half of 2011, consumer prices in Greater Algiers increased by 3.76% on a half-yearly average (6 months 2011/6 months 2010) against 4.62% in June 2010 bringing the price index to 141.1 points, base 100 in 2001. In June 2011, average annual inflation reached 3.49% compared to 5.41% a year earlier and the year-on-year price increase is estimated at 3.69% compared to 6.11% in June 2010. It is worth noting the sharp year-on-year increase in food prices (9.66% but 2.54% on an annual average), generated mainly by the increase in the prices of fresh agricultural products (14.9%) and to a lesser extent by that of industrial food products (5.6%). Finally, the government's measures to reduce the effect of imported inflation and to stem domestic market dysfunctions have been instrumental in mitigating the effect of the price shock at the beginning of the year on the general price level, even if markets remain insufficiently regulated in the context of adjustment to the rising incomes, fuelled by the fiscal sphere, and a corresponding expansion of financial savings of households and private enterprises. 7. Elements for improving the financing of the economy in 2011 In the perspective of sustainable growth driven by diversification, the rebalancing of the structure of the national economy favouring the development of agriculture, industry and productive services is necessary, in order to reduce its dependence on hydrocarbons and correspondingly on public expenditure. To achieve the potential for non-hydrocarbon growth in the medium term, the role of banks is now decisive in financing productive investments and non-hydrocarbon activities that create jobs. Anchored on a structural excess of savings over investment, such an allocation of available financial resources must be part of a dual objective of financial development, taking into account financial inclusion, and strong economic growth excluding hydrocarbons. This must be accompanied by a sustained improvement in the investment climate, especially since the use of the State's available financial savings to self-finance the public investment programme (capital expenditure) makes it possible to prevent any crowding-out effect. It is expected that banks, thanks to the State's support measures for SMEs in difficulty in repaying their bank debts, will examine, in the light of the measures relating to the rescheduling of these debts with a three-year deferral of repayment, the likelihood of improvement in their operation and the ability to upgrade during the three-year grace period during which interest on the debt will be paid by the Consolidated Revenue Fund. These new measures should help to improve the quality of bank loans and thereby establish the bank-enterprise relationship with a view to economic growth. In this regard, banks must now ensure better management of credit risks. Banks are encouraged to reschedule claims on SMEs in difficulty with a deferral of three (3) years during which the Treasury will bear the interest. In this perspective, the Council of Money and Credit issued in June 2011, in application of the provisions provided for in Article 62, paragraph j of Ordinance No. 03-11, amended and supplemented, relating to money and credit, a regulation which specifies that classified claims, objects of rescheduling, within the framework of the support granted by the State, are those recorded at the end of April 2011, net of uncollected interest. This Regulation establishes a framework for the treatment of uncollected interest recognised in respect of bank claims eligible for rescheduling for the benefit of small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) in difficulty, benefiting from the financial support of the State. This is a system in line with the prudential regulations in force. Finally, in order to ensure periodic follow-up in this area, banks and financial institutions are required to send to the Bank of Algeria, according to procedures that are defined by instruction, a statement of rescheduled claims benefiting from the support of the Treasury. These new support measures for SMEs (rescheduling of bank debts, assumption by the Treasury of interest due during the three-year deferral period, cancellation of unrecovered agios, subsidisation for investment loans and extension of deferral periods) would result in the reduction of financial charges for beneficiary SMEs and the consolidation of their asset situations (strengthening of their working capital). As a result, beneficiary SMEs are expected to seize this opportunity of financial relief to implement growth and sustainable development strategies for their production activities. Finally, favourable financial conditions and stronger financial soundness on the part of banks will contribute, from 2011 onwards, to further strengthening the role of the credit channel in the allocation of increased financial savings resources, in particular to productive investment. The current year recorded a trend towards improving certain performance indicators for companies benefiting from the new State financial support system, in a situation of better access to bank financing. As for bank intermediation for the benefit of the household sector, banks are expected to develop real estate loans to develop access to housing for this surplus economic agent whose contribution to the formation of national savings is very significant.

Pour les banques publiques, le rendement des actifs a lgrement baiss pour stablir  1,25 % en 2010 contre 1,33 % en 2009, du fait de limportance de leurs oprations avec la Banque dAlgrie qui sont moins bien rmunres. Pour ce qui est de la rentabilit des fonds propres des banques, elle a baiss tant pour les banques publiques que prives, baisse imputable  laugmentation substantielle de leurs fonds propres (capital plus rserves). Quant au ratio marge dintrt/revenu brut, il sest amlior en 2010 aussi bien pour les banques publiques que prives sous leffet de la hausse de marges dintrt nettes. Si les banques prives accroissent leur dpendance vis--vis des revenus hors intrt, ceux-ci servent  compenser la baisse de leur marge dintermdiation,  en juger par la baisse du ratio charges hors intrt / revenu brut qui passe de 52,73 % en 2009  39,24 % en 2010. La position de liquidit des banques est solide. Mesure par lun des indicateurs standards, la liquidit des banques est leve, comme en tmoigne labsence dendettement interbancaire et lintervention accrue de la Banque dAlgrie pour absorber dune manire effective lexcs de liquidit sur le march montaire. Cette situation traduit la capacit des banques  rembourser leurs engagements  court terme grce  des actifs liquides. Enfin, il ressort clairement de lanalyse des indicateurs de solidit financire que les banques publiques et prives, en dpit des diffrences constates, ont globalement enregistr au cours de lexercice 2010 une amlioration sensible de leurs rsultats (y incluses les provisions  caractre de rserves), grce en particulier  la rduction des charges du risque de crdit,  la diminution des dprciations dactifs et  la matrise des charges oprationnelles. Le secteur bancaire est, dans lensemble, solide et rsilient. 6. Principales tendances montaires et financires au premier semestre 2011 Au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord (MENA), les incertitudes au niveau global et les vnements rcents dans la rgion ont un impact ngatif sur l'activit conomique et la situation financire de certains pays, notamment en raison de la contraction des recettes de tourisme, des transferts des travailleurs  l'tranger, des flux de capitaux et d'investissement qui ont contribu au ralentissement de l'activit conomique et  la hausse du chmage, pendant que les pressions inflationnistes, inhrentes  la hausse des prix mondiaux des produits alimentaires et de l'nergie, se sont accrues. En ce qui concerne l'Algrie, l'importante pargne budgtaire et l'accroissement substantiel des rserves de change, lis au niveau lev des prix de ptrole, offrent une marge de manuvre apprciable Aussi, l'Algrie, tout en poursuivant l'expansion des dpenses en capital (d'investissement), a d recourir  l'augmentation des dpenses budgtaires courantes pour soutenir la demande intrieure et attnuer l'rosion du pouvoir d'achat des mnages, notamment les plus dmunis. Les mesures budgtaires prises ds le premier trimestre 2011 ont consist essentiellement en l'augmentation des subventions des prix des produits alimentaires et des transferts sociaux, notamment aux chmeurs, la suspension des taxes sur certains produits de base, la hausse des salaires, l'augmentation de l'emploi dans la fonction publique notamment des emplois non permanents et le financement bonifi du logement. La forte augmentation des dpenses courantes rsulte principalement de celle des dpenses de personnel et des transferts courants. Cette dernire rubrique s'tablit  1150,3 milliards de dinars au premier semestre de l'anne en cours, dcaisss principalement au second trimestre, et en accroissement de 70,3 % par rapport  leur montant du premier semestre de 2010 (675,6 milliards de dinars). En particulier, les subventions aux EPA sont en trs forte hausse ainsi que les diffrents autres soutiens pris en charge par le budget, tmoignant de l'effort accru de l'Etat en terme de couverture sociale en 2011. En consquence, le taux de couverture des dpenses de fonctionnement par les recettes hors hydrocarbures se situe  42,1 % au premier semestre 2011 contre 54,8 % en 2010, en contexte d'importance accrue des recettes budgtaires provenant des hydrocarbures. L'volution favorable des prix des hydrocarbures au premier semestre 2011 est aussi reflte par l'excdent apprciable du compte courant extrieur, soit un niveau meilleur par rapport aux performances semestrielles de l'anne passe. Les exportations hors hydrocarbures, en dpit de leur faiblesse structurelle, ont progress au premier semestre 2011, atteignant leur niveau de l'anne 2009 (0,77 milliard de dollars) contre 0,53 milliard de dollars pour le premier semestre 2010. En rythme semestriel, la hausse globale enregistre est de prs de 46 %. Quant aux importations de biens (fob), elles se sont accrues de 15,7 %, sous l'effet principalement de l'augmentation des importations de biens alimentaires et des biens de consommation, atteignant 22,37 milliards de dollars au premier semestre 2011 contre 19,33 milliards de dollars au cours de la mme priode de l'anne passe. Cette hausse porte plus particulirement sur les produits alimentaires (60,7 %). A titre d'exemple, les importations (caf) des trois principaux produits alimentaires (crales, lait et sucre) se sont leves  3,44 milliards de dollars au premier semestre 2011, soit quasiment la valeur des importations annuelles de 2010 (3,66 milliards de dollars) ; les crales reprsentant 59,4 % de ces importations. Si cette augmentation des importations des produits alimentaires de base rpond au souci d'une disponibilit accrue de ces produits sur le march domestique, elle rsulte notamment d'un fort effet prix inhrent aux importations des biens alimentaires et des biens de consommation. Pour ce qui est de l'ensemble des importations, elles ont enregistr une contraction en volume de prs de 9 % par rapport au premier semestre 2010. Pour ce qui est du compte de capital, il a enregistr au premier semestre 2011 une augmentation des flux dentre de capitaux au titre des IDE qui sont estim  1,331 milliard de dollars, en situation dimportants remboursements de dette extrieure notamment de court terme. Lencours de cette dernire est pass de 1,778 milliard de dollars  fin dcembre 2010  0,989 milliard de dollars  fin juin 2011. Au total, le solde global de la balance des paiements du premier semestre 2011 a atteint 9,11 milliards de dollars, soit plus de 4 milliards en rythme trimestriel. La position financire extrieure de l'Algrie sest ainsi consolide, en situation de recul de la dette extrieure et daccumulation soutenue des rserves de change (173,9 milliards de dollars  fin juin 2011, hors avoirs en DTS et or non compris). La gestion flexible du taux de change a eu pour rsultat le maintien du taux de change effectif rel du dinar quasiment  son niveau d'quilibre  moyen terme, en dpit de la volatilit accrue des cours de change des principales devises. En outre, le premier semestre 2011 est marqu par un amenuisement du diffrentiel d'inflation entre l'Algrie et ses principaux partenaires commerciaux. Les indicateurs de la situation montaire  fin juin 2011 montrent un accroissement relativement important de la masse montaire (8,62 %), principalement par la montisation des avoirs extrieurs, ainsi qu'une progression globalement significative des crdits  l'conomie (11,16 %). Ce trend confirme la poursuite du dynamisme des crdits  l'conomie et situant l'Algrie dans le groupe de pays mergents  croissance rapide du crdit. De plus, la hausse des crdits (hors obligations) concerne aussi bien les banques publiques (11,29 %) que les banques prives (16,44 %), pendant que son rythme est ingal entre les banques. Cependant, sous l'angle sectoriel, l'volution des crdits distribus par les banques est contraste au premier semestre 2011,  mesure que la hausse apprciable des crdits aux entreprises prives (10,21 %) s'est accompagne d'une hausse plus importante des crdits au secteur public (13,48 %) et une hausse modre des crdits aux mnages (3,47 %). Nanmoins, les crdits immobiliers aux mnages se sont accrus de 12,50 % et ont atteint 74 % du total des crdits aux mnages (68 %  fin 2010). La part des crdits au secteur priv (entreprises prives et mnages) dans le total des crdits distribus nets des rachats se stabilise au premier semestre (55,18 %). Paralllement, la part des crdits  court terme est en baisse au profit des crdits  moyen et long terme qui atteignent 62,57 % contre 59,89 %  fin dcembre 2010. Le dynamisme du financement  moyen et long terme de projets d'investissement, notamment en syndication bancaire, est ainsi confort et appuy par un rallongement des maturits de financement bancaire. Ce dernier phnomne se rvlera davantage au second semestre de 2011, sous l'effet de l'impulsion apporte par les pouvoirs publics (soutien financier). En outre, dans un contexte de forte croissance des crdits  l'conomie, le taux d'intrt moyen pondr par type de crdits a lgrement diminu au premier semestre par rapport  son niveau de fin 2010 et fin 2009. Ainsi, des conditions financires favorables et une solidit financire renforce des banques contribuent  conforter le rle du canal crdit dans l'allocation des ressources d'pargne financire accrues en 2011, qu'il s'agisse des dpts des mnages et entreprises prives ou des entreprises publiques, y compris celles des hydrocarbures. Pour les six premiers mois de 2011, les dpts  vue dans les banques se sont accrus de 6,55 %, soit un rythme infrieur  celui des dpts  terme (y compris les dpts en devises) (7,22 %), pendant que les dpts au CCP et au Trsor, quant  eux, enregistrent une hausse bien plus importante (21,84 %). Il importe de signaler galement une hausse importante de la monnaie fiduciaire  partir de 2007, soit  un rythme moyen annuel de 18,2 % pour les quatre dernires annes, dont le ratio par rapport  la masse montaire a atteint 26,09 %  fin juin 2011. Si ce ratio a t relativement stable entre 2005 et 2008,  environ 22 %, lenvole de la monnaie fiduciaire en circulation sexplique essentiellement par lampleur accrue des paiements en cash des transactions, au-del de celles relevant du commerce de dtail. En situation de stabilisation de leurs dpts en devises, l'importance accrue des dpts en dinars des mnages est alimente par l'augmentation des revenus salariaux et des transferts budgtaires. Il importe de souligner que les dpts en dinars des mnages atteignent 36,57 % de l'ensemble des dpts en dinars  fin juin 2011 et ils sont stables. Aussi, l'importante augmentation des avoirs financiers des agents  entreprises hors hydrocarbures et mnages  a aliment l'excs de liquidit des banques qui est rest structurel et, de plus, dissmin au niveau des banques. Pour sa part, la Banque d'Algrie a continu  rsorber l'excs de liquidit par des oprations de reprise  sept jours et trois mois, pendant que les banques ont rgulirement plac les montants en sus de l'objectif de constitution des rserves obligatoires en facilit de dpts rmunrs  24 heures. En consquence, le montant des rserves libres s'est contract au premier semestre 2011, refltant le caractre effectif de la rsorption de l'excs de liquidit par la Banque d'Algrie. Par ailleurs, au cours du premier semestre 2011, les banques ont consolid leurs indicateurs de solidit financire. En effet, le ratio de solvabilit reste apprciable  prs de 21 %, pendant que les deux ratios de liquidit sont levs comme  fin 2010. En outre, il importe de souligner que le niveau des crances non performantes dclares par les banques est en baisse passant de 19,05 % du total des crdits distribus  fin 2010  16,63 %  fin juin 2011. Cette amlioration est due  l'effet conjugu de la baisse du niveau des crances non performantes et de la hausse de l'encours des crdits distribus. Pour dvelopper davantage le cadre oprationnel de la stabilit financire et en phase avec les nouvelles normes du Comit de Ble, une rglementation en matire d'identification, mesure, gestion et contrle du risque de liquidit a t dicte par le Conseil de la monnaie et du crdit en mai 2011. En outre, ce rglement institue un coefficient de liquidit minimum que les banques et les tablissements financiers doivent respecter  tout moment. L'valuation faite par la Banque d'Algrie ds juin 2011 indique que les banques de la place satisfont  cette exigence ; cette anne se caractrisant par une liquidit bancaire plus ample et largement dissmine. Aussi, dans le but d'asseoir une meilleure pratique de gestion de liquidit et de suivi des oprations interbancaires et d'amliorer la qualit des reporting prudentiels, le Conseil de la monnaie et du crdit a galement dict en mai 2011 un second rglement instituant un systme de surveillance interne et de limitation par contrepartie des encours de prts et d'emprunts interbancaires, notamment ceux oprs sur le march montaire, que les banques et tablissements financiers sont tenus de mettre en place. Ces deux nouveaux dispositifs, qui viennent renforcer les instruments de supervision et de contrle, contribuent  renforcer davantage la stabilit et la solidit du systme bancaire algrien. Le suivi et le contrle de l'inflation mergent dsormais au premier plan en la matire, en application des nouvelles dispositions lgislatives relatives  la monnaie et au crdit (aot 2010). Au premier semestre 2011, la tendance haussire des rythmes dexpansion montaire conjugue  la hausse des cours des produits agricoles imports amplifie l'inflation des prix intrieurs. Au premier semestre 2011, les prix  la consommation dans le Grand Alger ont augment de 3,76 % en moyenne semestrielle (6 mois 2011/6 mois 2010) contre 4,62 % en juin 2010 portant l'indice des prix  141,1 points, base 100 en 2001. En juin 2011, l'inflation annuelle moyenne a atteint 3,49 % contre 5,41 % un an auparavant et la hausse des prix en glissement annuel est estime  3,69 % contre 6,11 % en juin 2010. Il faut relever la forte hausse des prix en glissement annuel des produits alimentaires (9,66 % mais 2,54 % en moyenne annuelle), gnre principalement par la hausse des prix des produits agricoles frais (14,9 %) et dans une moindre mesure par celle des produits alimentaires industriels (5,6 %). Enfin, les mesures prises par les pouvoirs publics visant  rduire l'effet de l'inflation importe et  endiguer les dysfonctionnements du march intrieur ont largement contribu  attnuer l'effet du choc des prix de dbut d'anne sur le niveau gnral des prix, mme si les marchs restent insuffisamment rguls en contexte d'ajustement  la hausse des revenus, alimente par la sphre budgtaire, et d'expansion corrlative des pargnes financires des mnages et entreprises prives. 7. Elments damlioration du financement de lconomie en 2011 Dans la perspective dune croissance durable porte par la diversification, le rquilibrage de la structure de lconomie nationale favorisant lessor de lagriculture, de lindustrie et des services productifs simpose, afin de rduire sa dpendance  lgard des hydrocarbures et corrlativement vis--vis de la dpense publique. Dans cette perspective, le Conseil de la monnaie et du crdit a dict en juin 2011, en application des dispositions prvues par larticle 62, alina j de lordonnance n 03-11, modifie et complte, relative  la monnaie et au crdit, un rglement qui prcise que les crances classes, objets de rchelonnement, dans le cadre du soutien consenti par lEtat, sont celles constates  fin avril 2011, nettes des intrts non recouvrs.
