Title: Statement to the International Monetary and Financial Committee on behalf of several countries
text: BANK OF ALGERIA Algiers, 25 August 2011 ECONOMIC AND MONETARY DEVELOPMENTS IN 2010 The purpose of this document is to explain the main conclusions of the Bank of Algeria's 2010 report on macroeconomic, financial and monetary developments for the year under review. Particular emphasis is placed on the main developments in the banking sector and on monetary policy. The annual report is provided for in Article 30 of the Ordinance on Money and Credit of 26 August 2003, as amended and supplemented. 1. Following the effect of the large external shock of 2009 inherent in the international financial crisis and the global economic crisis, the national economy achieved significant financial performance in 2010, including a consolidation of the net external financial position. Backed by the sustained recovery in the price of a barrel of oil in 2010 (80.15 against 62.26) and correspondingly to the sharp increase in hydrocarbon export earnings (26.4%), the current account balance recorded a significant surplus in 2010 (12.16 billion, 7.5% of GDP), in a situation of slight increase in imports (4%) where the relative share of capital goods and semi-finished products is close to two-thirds. This performance in the external current account benefited from the slight decline in the services deficit, the near equilibrium of the item (net) factor income in the context of appreciable income from the investment of foreign exchange reserves and the stabilization of the surplus of the current transfers (net). This confirmed the excess of saving over investment that characterized the 2000s, with the exception of 2009. After the external current account deficit in the first half of 2009, the surplus in 2010 is all the more appreciable as the current account balance becomes the pivotal element of Algeria's external balance of payments situation. The capital account, which, after the external deleveraging completed before the international financial crisis, is mainly limited to foreign direct investment (net), is also in surplus (3.4 billion). In particular, the latter recorded an improvement in 2010 (3.5 billion 1 2.5 billion in 2009), following a net capital outflow from foreign direct investment in selected sectors. As a result, the marked improvement in the overall external balance of payments surplus in 2010 (15.58 billion compared to 3.86 billion in 2009) fuelled Algeria's level of official foreign exchange reserves, which exceed three years (38.33 months) of imports of goods and services. The level of official foreign exchange reserves (including SDR holdings) stood at 162.22 billion at the end of 2010 (148.9 billion at the end of 2009), while medium- and long-term external debt stabilized (3.679 billion) and now represents only 2.27 percent of the estimated gross domestic product for 2010. These main parameters of Algeria's net external financial position confirm its solidity and strengthen its resilience to external shocks, especially since the Bank of Algeria's exchange rate management policy effectively contributes to external financial stability. In 2010, the intervention of the Bank of Algeria in the interbank foreign exchange market resulted in the appreciation of the real effective exchange rate of the dinar on an annual average (2.64%). The real effective exchange rate of the dinar remained almost at equilibrium in the medium term, despite the increased volatility of the exchange rates of the main currencies and the structural weakness of non-hydrocarbon exports (about one billion dollars in 2010). The structure of external payments indicates that the share of payments in euros stabilizes at 46% against 50% for the dollar; the structure of foreign trade with Algeria's fifteen main trading partners serving as the basis for weighting the real effective exchange rate and the basket of reference currencies. In this context, the level of official foreign exchange reserves is of particular importance as it is the main bulwark against possible external shocks. Thus, external financial stability in the medium and long term is strongly based on the continued prudent management of official foreign exchange reserves by the Bank of Algeria. The objectives pursued in this area are to: - Preserve the value of capital: minimize the risk of loss of the market value of assets, maintaining a diversified portfolio of high-quality assets (in terms of credit rating and type of issuer) and applying appropriate risk mitigation practices; - Maintain a high level of liquidity: place reserves in assets that mature or can be resold quickly without loss of value; - Optimize returns: obtain the best possible return while respecting the objectives of security and liquidity. 2 As a result, while deposits have been made particularly with central banks and supranational financial institutions since 2007, securities portfolios, whose share has since increased to an average of 98% of total reserves, are invested in best-rated and therefore least risky instruments, mainly sovereign bonds. In terms of returns, the Investments made by the Bank of Algeria in securities portfolios during the years when interest rates were high continue to generate relatively high returns, at nearly 3% in 2010 and above 3% in 2008 and 2009. These performances are all the more appreciable as they are achieved in the context of very low interest rates in advanced countries and key rates close to zero, particularly in the United States. In addition, it is important to stress that real rates of return remain positive. The diversification initiated since 2004, both in terms of the choice of currencies used in the composition of reserves and their distribution at the portfolio level, and in terms of securities, by risk class, has contributed to this performance, while minimizing risks. The objective of security remains paramount, especially since the international environment was marked in 2010 by the emergence of sovereign debt risks in a context of rising banking risks. 2. While the average annual inflation differential between Algeria and the euro area has narrowed, while still remaining high, the appreciation of the real effective exchange rate of the dinar has helped to limit the impact of imported inflation on the general price level, especially since the prices of consumer goods with a high import content recorded a strong increase in 2010 (7%). The increase in international prices of imported agricultural commodities (cereals and tropical products), the increase in the money supply and the increase in the wholesale prices of fresh fruit and vegetables are the main factors that explain and determine inflation, with contributions estimated at 31%, 62% and 7% respectively on average over the decade. It is important here to highlight the inflationary impact of the dysfunctions of the internal markets. Indeed, for the first time in five years, the average annual inflation rate measured by the consumer price index fell from 6.1% in 2009 to 4.1% for the national index and from 5.7% in 2009 to 3.9% for the Greater Algiers index. In contrast to previous years, inflation in 2010 is mainly driven by higher prices for services and manufactured goods, although food goods have experienced substantial increases, which are significantly lower than in the past. While since 2003, the rise in consumer prices has been lower in Algeria than in the MENA region and below the median inflation for all these years, the slowdown in the growth rate of industrial producer prices since 2008 and consumer prices in 2010 suggests that a disinflation dynamic is underway in 3 Algeria, a dynamic that must be reinforced by controlling the main determinants of inflation: non-hydrocarbon money creation in line with real growth, control of rising factor costs and stimulation of supply. 3. Thus, after two years of moderate economic activity at 2.4%, the recovery in growth, driven by domestic demand, itself supported by the increase in resources, was confirmed in 2010 (3.3%), while the hydrocarbon sector has recorded negative growth since 2006. Indeed, all sectors of activity other than hydrocarbons experienced positive growth, with a weak performance of industry (0.9% against 5% in 2009) and agriculture (6.0% against 20.0% in 2009); non-hydrocarbon GDP in volume terms grew by 6.0% in 2010 (9.3% in 2009). The appreciable growth excluding hydrocarbons, unevenly distributed by sector, is driven by the increase in the contribution of the market services sectors, in particular trade and transport, non-market and construction, in the context of declines in those of manufacturing and agriculture. At the same time, growth in domestic expenditure has slowed, but remains high at 5.5% in volume terms in 2010, driven by strong growth in household and general government spending, confirming the role of public spending as a decisive stimulus for economic activity in Algeria. While total budgetary expenditure increased by 6.3% in 2010, after its quasi-stabilisation in 2009, capital expenditure fell in both 2009 and 2010 by 1.4% and 6% respectively, after its strong increase since 2005. Their growth rate peaked at 41.3 per cent in 2007 (37.5 per cent in 2008). Also, after many years of upward developments, the ratio of capital expenditure to GDP fell from 19.4% in 2009 to 15.1% in 2010, reflecting the significant slowdown in capital absorption. The ratio of current expenditure to GDP stabilised in 2010 (22.2% compared with 22.9% in 2009), while the increase in current expenditure resulted in particular from that of staff costs. In addition, the rate of coverage of operating expenses by non-hydrocarbon revenues remained stable in 2010 (54.8%), after a decrease from 2006 to 2008. In 2010, hydrocarbon revenues increased by 20.4% to 66.3% of total budgetary revenues and covering 64.4% of total budgetary expenditures. Non-hydrocarbon revenues, representing 33.6 per cent of total budget revenues, increased by 16.5 per cent (14.6 per cent in 2009), while the relative share of tax revenues was 87.6 per cent. Moreover, while the ratio of non-hydrocarbon revenues to non-hydrocarbon gross domestic product remained stable in 2010 (18.7%), this stability should not overshadow the change in the structure of non-hydrocarbon taxation during the years 2004-2010. Indeed, levies on income, 4 corporate wages and profits have grown relatively faster than levies on economic activity (taxes on goods and services and customs duties), despite the substantial increase in the latter's base. In total, after nearly a decade of surpluses, the overall balance of Treasury operations is in deficit for the second consecutive year (0.9% of GDP in 2010 and 7.1% in 2009). Despite this deficit, the Treasury's financing capacity consolidated in 2010, judging by the outstanding resources of the revenue regulation fund, which increased by 526.4 billion dinars to 40.1% of gross domestic product. This strengthens the sustainability of public finances, despite the increase in domestic public debt in 2010. The effectiveness of public investment must now be the ultimate goal. Particular attention should be paid to the content of investment capacity building. 4. The resumption in 2010 of the increase in accumulated resources (financial savings) in the Revenue Regulation Fund, despite the strong increase in current budgetary expenditure (personnel costs and transfers) compared to its evolution in 2009, helped to mitigate monetisation. The analysis of the sources of money creation in 2010 confirms that external assets (in foreign currency) constitute the essential element in this process and therefore in the formation of the financial savings of non-financial economic agents. Thus, the outstanding net foreign assets of the Bank of Algeria expressed in dinars, i.e. 11854.02 billion at the end of 2010, was monetized at 72.4% (excluding valuation). Given the weakness of banks' net foreign assets, the additional money creation is represented by loans to the economy (3671.1 billion dinars) distributed by banks and financial institutions. As a result, all these assets, consisting mainly of external assets (foreign exchange reserves), are matched by the outstanding financial savings (deposits in banks and fiat money) of companies and households (8323.28 billion dinars at the end of 2010) and the outstanding financial savings (revenue regulation fund and other current account deposits at the Bank of Algeria and banks) of the State (5108.13 billion dinars at the end of 2010). It is in such a context of development of financial savings that the combined effect of sterilization by the Treasury and the absorption of excess liquidity by the Bank of Algeria contributed to further anchoring monetary and financial stability in 2010, despite the resumption of the expansion of the M2 money supply (13.8%). After a historically low monetary expansion recorded in 2009 (3.1%) as a result of the large external shock, 2010 was marked by a return to monetary expansion, but at a rate lower than the high rates of the years 2006 to 2008. With a 5 an increase of 10.2% in 2010, the resumption of the role of net foreign assets in the money creation process was combined with the continued dynamism of credit to the economy. Contrary to the situation in several emerging countries that have recorded a contraction in credit to the economy linked to the international financial crisis, loans distributed by banks operating in Algeria to companies and households, directly or through investment in bonds issued by companies, increased by 15.6% in 2010 (excluding the purchase of non-performing loans by the Treasury). This increase corresponds to a strong growth in loans, in real terms, during 2010, placing Algeria in the group of emerging countries with rapid credit growth. As a result of the strong growth in medium- and long-term loans, the share of these loans rose to 59.9% at the end of 2010 compared to 57.2% at the end of 2009, confirming the long-term financing momentum of investment projects, particularly in bank syndication, and thus contributing to the extension of bank financing maturities. In Algeria, favourable financial conditions and the resilience of the banking system in the face of the external shock have helped to strengthen the role of the credit channel in the allocation of savings resources; these consolidated during 2010, both in the hydrocarbon sector and in other sectors of activity, after the contraction of deposits in the hydrocarbon sector in 2009. It is worth noting that at the end of 2010, the outstanding financial savings of private households and enterprises exceeded that of public enterprises, including hydrocarbons. As a result, the substantial increase in bank deposits (sight and term in dinars) in 2010, 12.5% compared to a decrease of 8.2% in 2009, helped to further consolidate the banks' lending fund capacity, anchored on stable and increased resources and a good liquidity position. In addition, excess liquidity is increasingly scattered at the level of the banks of the place. This has, however, led to less dynamic activity in the interbank money market. Indeed, having stable financial resources enabling them to carry out their various activities in a context of low liquidity risk, banks have only rarely intervened on the money market to obtain liquidity during 2010, in particular to meet the objectives of setting up regulatory minimum reserves. Despite the acuteness of the excess structural liquidity fuelled by the significant recovery in monetary growth in 2010, the orderly conduct of monetary policy by the Bank of Algeria helped to contain inflationary pressures in 2010 and thus further establish monetary stability. The effective conduct of monetary policy has been based on the effective absorption of excess liquidity, given the magnitude of the monetization of external assets, which increased significantly in 2010 after the external shock of 2009. 6 In addition, if free reserves constituted on average an amount of 63 billion dinars in 2010, it is important to note that of this amount, the free deposits of banks, which do not intervene in operations with the Bank of Algeria, reach 54 billion dinars. Also, after an adjustment in 2009 of the regulatory framework for monetary policy instruments (liquidity recovery, interest-bearing deposit facility and minimum reserves), 2010 was marked by the reform of the relevant legal framework where the inflation target was established as the ultimate objective of monetary policy, while maintaining quantitative monetary objectives. This de facto gives a role to monetary and credit aggregates in the conduct of monetary policy by the Bank of Algeria, while the forecast of short-term inflation now takes on particular importance. Inflation forecasting and its monitoring has led the Bank of Algeria to develop an adequate tool since September 2009, namely a short-term inflation forecasting model responding to the concern for a forward-looking vision, in order to forecast the inflation rate and its evolution over a one-year horizon on a monthly basis. For example, the forecast of annual average inflation for the end of 2010 made in September 2010 differs only 0.14 percentage points from the inflation rate achieved and calculated by the ONS for December (3.91%). As a result, average annual inflation remained close to short-term forecasts. This inflation rate is down compared to the rise in prices at the end of 2009 (5.74%) and in line with the inflation target set by the Currency and Credit Council (4%, or d0 1 point) for the year 2010, as the implicit objective of monetary policy. 5. The contribution of monetary policy to financial stability remains decisive in Algeria, given the predominance of banks in the Algerian financial system. In 2010, the banking sector remains strong, anchored on stable and increased resources and a very strong liquidity position of banks. While banks' activity is mainly driven by the credit segment, the soundness of the banking sector is appreciable both in terms of the evolution of their activities and in terms of the return on equity and return on assets. The indicators of soundness of both public and private banks are close to those recorded in emerging countries: the solvency ratio is comfortable (23.31% in 2010 against 22.11% in 2009), well beyond the recommendations of Bale III, the return on equity is substantial (20.72% in 2010) and the return on assets is substantial (1.52%), corresponding to the best results achieved in emerging countries. Banks' interest margins are increasing (63.80% in 2010) 7 compared to 57.36% in 2009), in line with the decrease in non-interest expenses (39.40% in 2010 compared to 49.98% in 2009). In terms of credit portfolio quality, banks have taken care to strengthen credit risk management. The gross rate of non-performing loans at the end of 2010 is declining, although the level of these receivables remains higher than international standards in this area. Non-performing loans are heavily provisioned (74.1% compared to 68.3% at the end of 2009) indicating that banks, both public and private, while increasing their own funds, have ensured that the necessary provisions are made. Finally, the new provisions on currency and credit of August 2010 strengthened the Bank of Algeria's missions in terms of supervision and banking supervision and assigned it new prerogatives in the area of financial stability. In this context, the Bank of Algeria has consolidated its stress testing capabilities, in parallel with the finalization of the new rating system for banks and financial institutions, from the perspective of better control of banking risks (risk-based supervision). All in all, the Bank of Algeria must ensure the security and soundness of the banking system, a prerequisite for an efficient allocation of resources for the benefit of productive investment, given the persistence of the excess of savings over investment. In the perspective of sustainable growth driven by diversification, the rebalancing of the structure of the national economy favouring the development of agriculture, industry and productive services is necessary, in order to reduce its dependence on hydrocarbons and correspondingly on public expenditure. To achieve the potential for non-hydrocarbon growth in the medium term, the role of banks is now decisive in financing productive investments and non-hydrocarbon activities that create jobs. Such an allocation of available financial resources must be part of a dual objective of financial development, taking into account financial inclusion, and strong non-hydrocarbon economic growth. This must be accompanied by a sustained improvement in the investment climate, especially since the use of the State's available financial savings to self-finance the public investment programme (capital expenditure) makes it possible to prevent any crowding-out effect. 8

Ces principaux paramtres de la position financire extrieure nette de lAlgrie confirment sa solidit et confortent sa rsilience face aux chocs extrieurs, dautant que la politique de gestion du taux de change par la Banque d'Algrie contribue de manire effective  la stabilit financire externe. En 2010, l'intervention de la Banque d'Algrie sur le march interbancaire des changes a eu pour rsultat lapprciation du taux de change effectif rel du dinar en moyenne annuelle (2,64 %). Le taux de change effectif rel du dinar est rest quasiment  son niveau d'quilibre  moyen terme, en dpit de la volatilit accrue des cours de change des principales devises et de la faiblesse structurelle des exportations hors hydrocarbures (environ un milliard de dollars en 2010). La structure des paiements extrieurs indique que la part des paiements en euro se stabilise  46 % contre 50 % pour le dollar ; la structure du commerce extrieur avec les quinze principaux partenaires commerciaux de lAlgrie servant de base de pondration du taux de change effectif rel et du panier de monnaies de rfrence. Dans ce contexte, le niveau des rserves officielles de change revt une importance particulire dans la mesure o il constitue le principal rempart contre dventuels chocs extrieurs. Ainsi, la stabilit financire externe sur le moyen et long terme repose fortement sur la poursuite de la gestion prudente des rserves officielles de change par la Banque dAlgrie. Les objectifs poursuivis en la matire consistent  : - Prserver la valeur du capital : minimiser le risque de perte de la valeur marchande des actifs, en maintenant un portefeuille diversifi dactifs de haute qualit (en terme de notation de crdit et de type dmetteur) et en appliquant des pratiques appropries dattnuation des risques ; - Maintenir un niveau lev de liquidit : placer les rserves dans des actifs qui viennent  chance ou peuvent tre revendus rapidement sans perte de valeur ; - Optimiser le rendement : obtenir le meilleur rendement possible tout en respectant les objectifs de scurit et de liquidit. 2 En consquence, si les dpts sont effectus particulirement auprs des banques centrales et des institutions financires supranationales depuis 2007, les portefeuilles en titres, dont la part sest accrue depuis et a atteint 98 % en moyenne du total des rserves, sont investis dans des instruments bnficiant de la meilleure notation et donc les moins risqus, principalement les titres souverains. Pour ce qui est du rendement, les investissements effectus par la Banque dAlgrie en portefeuilles titres durant les annes o les taux d'intrt taient hauts continuent  gnrer des rendements relativement levs,  savoir prs de 3 % en 2010 et suprieurs  3 % en 2008 et 2009. Ces performances sont dautant plus apprciables quelles sont ralises en contexte de taux dintrt trs bas dans les pays avancs et de taux directeurs proches de zro notamment aux Etats Unis. En outre, il importe de souligner que les taux de rendement rels restent positifs. La diversification engage depuis 2004, tant sur le plan du choix des devises entrant dans la composition des rserves et leur distribution au niveau des portefeuilles, que sous langle titres, par classe de risque, a contribu  cette performance, tout en minimisant les risques. Lobjectif de scurit reste primordial, dautant que lenvironnement international a t marqu en 2010 par lapparition des risques lis  la dette souveraine en contexte de risques bancaires  la hausse. 2. Si le diffrentiel d'inflation annuelle moyenne entre l'Algrie et la zone euro sest rduit, tout en restant encore lev, lapprciation du taux de change effectif rel du dinar a contribu  limiter limpact de linflation importe sur le niveau gnral des prix, dautant que les prix des biens de consommation  fort contenu d'importation ont enregistr une forte progression en 2010 (7 %). La hausse des cours internationaux des produits agricoles de base imports (crales et produits tropicaux), laccroissement de la masse montaire ainsi que la hausse des prix de gros des fruits et lgumes frais sont les principaux facteurs qui expliquent et dterminent linflation, avec des contributions respectives estimes  31 %, 62 % et 7 % en moyenne sur la dcennie. Il importe ici de souligner limpact inflationniste des dysfonctionnements des marchs intrieurs. En effet, pour la premire fois depuis cinq ans, le taux dinflation annuel moyen mesur par lindice des prix  la consommation a flchi, passant de 6,1 % en 2009  4,1 % pour lindice national et de 5,7 % en 2009  3,9 % pour lindice du Grand Alger. Contrairement aux annes prcdentes, linflation en 2010 est principalement gnre par la hausse des prix des services et des biens manufacturs, mme si les biens alimentaires ont subi des hausses substantielles, au demeurant nettement plus faibles que par le pass. Si depuis 2003, la hausse des prix  la consommation a t plus faible en Algrie que dans la rgion MENA et infrieure  linflation mdiane pour toutes ces annes, le ralentissement du taux de croissance des prix  la production industrielle depuis 2008 et des prix  la consommation en 2010 laisse penser quune dynamique de dsinflation est engage en 3 Algrie, dynamique quil convient de conforter par la matrise des principaux dterminants de linflation : cration montaire hors hydrocarbures en phase avec la croissance relle, matrise de la hausse des cots des facteurs et stimulation de loffre. 3. Aussi, aprs deux annes dactivit conomique  rythme modr  2,4 %, la reprise de la croissance, tire par la demande intrieure, elle mme soutenue par laccroissement des ressources, se confirme en 2010 (3,3 %), pendant que le secteur des hydrocarbures enregistre une croissance ngative depuis 2006. En effet, tous les secteurs dactivit autres que celui des hydrocarbures ont connu une croissance positive, avec une faible performance de lindustrie (0,9 % contre 5 % en 2009) et lagriculture (6,0 % contre 20,0 % en 2009) ; le PIB hors hydrocarbures en volume progressant  hauteur de 6,0 % en 2010 (9,3 % en 2009). La croissance apprciable hors hydrocarbures, ingalement rpartie par secteur, est porte par laccroissement de la contribution des secteurs des services marchands, notamment commerce et transport, non marchands et du BTP, en contexte de recul de celles de lindustrie manufacturire et de lagriculture. Paralllement, la croissance de la dpense intrieure sest rduite, mais demeure leve  5,5 % en volume en 2010, impulse par la forte progression des dpenses des mnages et des administrations publiques, confirmant le rle des dpenses publiques comme stimulant dcisif de lactivit conomique en Algrie. Si les dpenses budgtaires totales ont progress de 6,3 % en 2010, aprs leur quasi stabilisation en 2009, les dpenses dquipement ont recul aussi bien en 2009 quen 2010 respectivement de 1,4 % et 6 %, aprs leur forte progression depuis lanne 2005. Leur taux de croissance avait culmin  41,3 % en 2007 (37,5 % en 2008). Aussi, aprs de nombreuses annes dvolution haussire, le ratio dpenses dquipement / PIB a baiss, passant de 19,4 % en 2009  15,1 % en 2010, tmoignant du ralentissement sensible de labsorption en la matire. Quant au ratio dpenses courantes/PIB, il sest stabilis en 2010 (22,2 % contre 22,9 % en 2009), pendant que laugmentation des dpenses courantes a rsult notamment de celle des dpenses de personnel. En outre, le taux de couverture des dpenses de fonctionnement par les recettes hors hydrocarbures est rest stable en 2010 (54,8 %), aprs une baisse de 2006  2008. En 2010, les recettes des hydrocarbures ont augment de 20,4 %, stablissant  66,3 % des recettes budgtaires totales et couvrant 64,4 % des dpenses budgtaires totales. Quant aux recettes hors hydrocarbures, reprsentant 33,6 % du total des recettes budgtaires, elles ont progress de 16,5 % (14,6 % en 2009), pendant que la part relative des recettes fiscales est de 87,6 %. Par ailleurs, si le ratio recettes hors hydrocarbures/produit intrieur brut hors hydrocarbures est rest stable en 2010 (18,7 %), cette stabilit ne doit pas occulter le changement de structure de la fiscalit hors hydrocarbures au cours des annes 2004-2010. En effet, les prlvements sur les revenus, 4 salaires et bnfices des socits ont augment relativement plus vite que les prlvements sur lactivit conomique (impts sur les biens et services et droits de douane), en dpit de laccroissement substantiel de lassiette de ces derniers. Au total, aprs prs dune dcennie dexcdents, le solde global des oprations du Trsor est dficitaire pour la deuxime anne conscutive (0,9 % du PIB en 2010 et 7,1 % en 2009). Malgr ce dficit, la capacit de financement du Trsor sest consolide en 2010,  en juger par lencours des ressources du fonds de rgulation des recettes qui sest accru de 526,4 milliards de dinars pour atteindre 40,1 % du produit intrieur brut. Cela renforce la viabilit des finances publiques, en dpit de laugmentation de la dette publique intrieure en 2010. Lefficacit de linvestissement public doit tre dsormais lobjectif ultime. Une attention particulire doit tre accorde au renforcement contenu des capacits dinvestir. 4. La reprise en 2010 de laccroissement des ressources accumules (pargnes financires) dans le Fonds de rgulation des recettes, en dpit de la forte progression des dpenses budgtaires courantes (dpenses du personnel et transferts) comparativement  leur volution en 2009, a contribu  attnuer la montisation. Lanalyse des sources de cration montaire en 2010 confirme que les avoirs extrieurs (en devises) constituent llment essentiel dans ce processus et donc dans la formation des pargnes financires des agents conomiques non financiers. Ainsi, lencours des avoirs extrieurs nets de la Banque dAlgrie exprims en dinars, soit 11854,02 milliards  fin 2010, a t montis  hauteur de 72,4 % (hors valorisation). Vu la faiblesse des avoirs extrieurs nets des banques, le complment de cration montaire est reprsent par les crdits  lconomie (3671,1 milliards de dinars) distribus par les banques et tablissements financiers. En consquence, lensemble de ces actifs, constitus principalement davoirs extrieurs (rserves de change), ont pour contrepartie lencours des pargnes financires (dpts dans les banques et monnaie fiduciaire) des entreprises et mnages (8323,28 milliards de dinars  fin 2010) et lencours de lpargne financire (fonds de rgulation des recettes et autres dpts en comptes courants  la Banque dAlgrie et les banques) de lEtat (5108,13 milliards de dinars  fin 2010). Cest dans un tel contexte de dveloppement de lpargne financire, que leffet conjugu de la strilisation par le Trsor et de labsorption de lexcs de liquidit par la Banque dAlgrie a contribu  ancrer davantage la stabilit montaire et financire en 2010, malgr la reprise de lexpansion de la masse montaire M2 (13,8 %). Aprs une expansion montaire historiquement basse enregistre en 2009 (3,1 %) sous leffet de limportant choc externe, lanne 2010 a t marque par le retour  lexpansion montaire, mais  un taux infrieur aux rythmes levs des annes 2006  2008. Avec une 5 progression de 10,2 % en 2010, la reprise du rle des avoirs extrieurs nets dans le processus de cration montaire sest conjugue avec la poursuite du dynamisme des crdits  lconomie. Contrairement  la situation de plusieurs pays mergents qui ont enregistr une contraction des crdits  lconomie lie  la crise financire internationale, les crdits distribus par les banques oprant en Algrie aux entreprises et mnages, directement ou par le biais de linvestissement en obligations mises par les entreprises, ont augment de 15,6 % en 2010 (hors rachat de crdits non performants par le Trsor). Cette hausse correspond  une forte croissance des crdits, en termes rels, au cours de lanne 2010, situant lAlgrie dans le groupe de pays mergents  croissance rapide du crdit. Sous leffet de la forte croissance des crdits  moyen et long termes, la part de ces crdits est monte  59,9 %  fin 2010 contre 57,2 %  fin 2009, confirmant la dynamique de financement  long terme de projets d'investissement notamment en syndication bancaire et contribuant ainsi au rallongement des maturits de financement bancaire. En Algrie, des conditions financires favorables et une rsilience du systme bancaire face au choc externe ont contribu  renforcer le rle du canal crdit dans lallocation des ressources dpargne ; celles-ci stant consolides au cours de lanne 2010, tant au niveau du secteur des hydrocarbures que des autres secteurs dactivit, aprs la contraction des dpts du secteur des hydrocarbures en 2009. Il est utile de noter qu fin 2010, lencours de lpargne financire des mnages et entreprises prives excde celui des entreprises publiques, y compris celles des hydrocarbures. En consquence, laugmentation substantielle des dpts bancaires ( vue et  terme en dinars) en 2010, 12,5 % contre une baisse de 8,2 % en 2009, a contribu  consolider davantage la capacit de fonds prtables des banques, ancre sur des ressources stables et accrues et une bonne position de liquidit. De plus, lexcs de liquidit est de plus en plus dissmin au niveau des banques de la place. Cela a, cependant, induit une activit moins dynamique sur le march montaire interbancaire. En effet, disposant de ressources financires stables leur permettant de mener leurs diffrentes activits en contexte de faible risque de liquidit, les banques ne sont intervenues que rarement sur le march montaire pour se procurer de la liquidit au cours de lanne 2010, notamment pour rpondre aux objectifs de constitution de rserves obligatoires rglementaires. En dpit de lacuit de lexcs de liquidit structurel aliment par la reprise significative de la croissance montaire en 2010, la conduite ordonne de la politique montaire par la Banque dAlgrie a contribu  contenir les pressions inflationnistes en 2010 et donc  asseoir davantage la stabilit montaire. La conduite efficace de la politique montaire a repos sur la rsorption effective de lexcs de liquidit, vu lampleur de la montisation des avoirs extrieurs qui se sont nettement accrus en 2010 aprs le choc externe de 2009. 6 De plus, si les rserves libres ont constitu en moyenne un montant de 63 milliards de dinars en 2010, il importe de noter que sur ce montant, les dpts libres des banques, qui ninterviennent pas dans les oprations avec la Banque dAlgrie, atteignent 54 milliards de dinars. Aussi, aprs un ajustement en 2009 du dispositif rglementaire portant instruments de conduite de la politique montaire (reprises de liquidit, facilit de dpts rmunrs et rserves obligatoires), lanne 2010 a t marque par la rforme du cadre lgal en la matire o lobjectif dinflation a t institu en tant quobjectif ultime de la politique montaire, tout en conservant les objectifs quantitatifs montaires. Ce qui confre de facto un rle aux agrgats montaires et de crdit dans la conduite de la politique montaire par la Banque dAlgrie, pendant que la prvision de linflation  court terme prend dsormais une importance particulire. La prvision de linflation et son monitoring a amen la Banque dAlgrie  dvelopper un outil adquat depuis septembre 2009,  savoir un modle de prvision de linflation  court terme rpondant au souci dune vision prospective, afin de prvoir mensuellement le taux dinflation et son volution dans un horizon dune anne. A titre dexemple, la prvision de linflation en moyenne annuelle pour fin 2010 effectue en septembre 2010 ne diffre que de 0,14 point de pourcentage du taux dinflation ralis et calcul par lONS pour dcembre (3,91 %). En consquence, linflation annuelle moyenne est reste proche des prvisions  court terme. Ce taux dinflation est en recul par rapport  la hausse des prix  fin 2009 (5,74 %) et en phase avec lobjectif dinflation arrt par le Conseil de la monnaie et du crdit (4 %, + ou  1 point) au titre de lanne 2010, comme objectif implicite de la politique montaire. 5. La contribution de la politique montaire  la stabilit financire reste dcisive en Algrie, vu la prdominance des banques dans le systme financier algrien. En 2010, le secteur bancaire reste solide, ancr sur des ressources stables et accrues et une position de liquidit des banques trs solide. Si lactivit des banques est principalement tire par le segment activit de crdits, la solidit du secteur bancaire est apprciable aussi bien sous langle de lvolution de leurs activits quen ce qui concerne la rentabilit de leurs fonds propres (return on equity) et du rendement de leurs actifs (return on assets). Les indicateurs de solidit aussi bien des banques publiques que prives sont proches de ceux enregistrs dans les pays mergents : le ratio de solvabilit est confortable (23,31 % en 2010 contre 22,11 % en 2009), bien au-del des recommandations de Bale III, la rentabilit des fonds propres est substantielle (20,72 % en 2010) et le rendement des actifs est consquent (1,52 %), correspondant aux meilleurs rsultats raliss dans les pays mergents. La marge dintrt des banques est en hausse (63,80 % en 2010 7 contre 57,36 % en 2009), en phase avec la baisse des charges hors intrt (39,40 % en 2010 contre 49,98 % en 2009). Sur le plan de la qualit de portefeuille de crdit, les banques ont veill  renforcer la gestion de risques de crdit. Le taux brut de crances non performantes  fin 2010 est en baisse, bien que le niveau de ces crances reste plus lev que les standards internationaux en la matire. Les crances non performantes sont fortement provisionnes (74,1 % contre 68,3 %  fin 2009) indiquant que les banques, publiques et prives, tout en augmentant leurs fonds propres ont veill  constituer les provisionnements ncessaires. Enfin, les nouvelles dispositions relatives  la monnaie et au crdit daot 2010 ont renforc les missions de la Banque dAlgrie en matire de supervision et de contrle bancaire et lui ont assign des prrogatives nouvelles en matire de stabilit financire. Dans ce cadre, la Banque dAlgrie a consolid ses capacits en matire de stress tests, paralllement  la finalisation du nouveau systme de notation des banques et tablissements financiers, sous langle dun meilleur contrle des risques bancaires (une supervision oriente sur les risques). Au total, la Banque dAlgrie doit sassurer de la scurit et de la solidit du systme bancaire, un pr requis pour une allocation efficace des ressources au profit de linvestissement productif, vu la persistance de lexcs de lpargne sur linvestissement. Dans la perspective dune croissance durable porte par la diversification, le rquilibrage de la structure de lconomie nationale favorisant lessor de lagriculture, de lindustrie et des services productifs simpose, afin de rduire sa dpendance  lgard des hydrocarbures et corrlativement vis--vis de la dpense publique. Pour atteindre le potentiel de croissance hors hydrocarbures sur le moyen terme, le rle des banques est dsormais dcisif en matire de financement des investissements productifs et des activits hors hydrocarbures cratrices demplois. Une telle allocation des ressources financires disponibles doit sinscrire dans un double objectif de dveloppement financier, prenant en compte linclusion financire, et de forte croissance conomique hors hydrocarbures. Cela doit tre accompagn par une amlioration soutenue du climat des investissements, dautant que lutilisation des pargnes financires disponibles de lEtat pour autofinancer le programme dinvestissements publics (dpenses dquipement) permet de prvenir tout effet dviction. 8

Title: Intervention before the APN on monetary and financial developments in 2017 and trends for the 2018 financial year
text: BANK OF ALGERIA Message from the Governor at the opening of the Day on: "Bank Modernization: Achievements and Prospects" Organised by ABEF 19 February 2019  Mr. Minister,  Mr. President of ABEF,  Presidents and Directors General  Honorable assistance, First of all, I would like to thank the organizers of this meeting for granting me the privilege of addressing the banking and financial community on a theme that challenges us all, especially at a time when the role of banks in the sound and sustainable financing of the economy is more crucial than ever. As everyone knows, the financing of the Algerian economy remains largely dominated by public spending, which is itself dependent, to a large extent, on oil taxation. Recent history has highlighted the consequences for the economy that a difficult public finance situation could have. The use of non-conventional financing, in the absence of other sources of financing, has made it possible to loosen this financial constraint and ensure the continuity of public expenditure, but this cannot constitute a lasting solution, as rightly recognised by the legal provisions establishing this type of financing. Indeed, in accordance with those same provisions, the use of this financing mechanism is limited in time and backed by the objective of restoring macroeconomic balances and anchoring a process of diversification of the economy, through a wide spectrum of economic, institutional and financial reforms. In this range of reforms, the reform and modernization of the banking sector is paramount. Public investment has contributed to the provision of basic infrastructure to the national economy for the creation and development of enterprises. They constitute an important basis for the development of market productive investment, in order to generate sustainable, endogenous, self-sustaining and inclusive growth. Market productive investment must rise and extend, much more than in the past, to activities in manufacturing industries and market productive services, the basis of which is constituted, in Algeria, as elsewhere, by small and medium-sized enterprises, the main providers of employment. Supporting this investment with adequate financing is crucial for the successful diversification of the economy. The role of banks in this regard is paramount. But the financial market, hitherto embryonic, must also play its role. The channelling of large economic groups to this market, for part of their financing needs, would contribute to its strong dynamism and would open up more space for bank financing of SMEs. In the banking sphere, the reform of bank governance must be a major strategic axis, guided by the principles of autonomy, efficiency and performance obligation. It must be a strong signal of the direction of the necessary banking reforms, capable of promoting competition and greater efficiency in bank intermediation. The collection of resources is one of the Achilles heels of the Algerian banking system. Of the approximately 5,000 billion dinars of fiat money in circulation, which represents nearly 32% of the M2 money supply, it is estimated that between 1,500 and 2,000 billion dinars represent the savings, excluding banking circuits, of economic agents. The improvement of existing banking services and an aggressive policy of offering innovative services, including a policy of attractive rates, would certainly make it possible to drain a large part of this savings into banking channels. This approach is all the more necessary since the current ease in terms of bank liquidity is generated, to a large extent, by monetary financing, which is due to end within a limited time horizon. The Bank of Algeria remains attentive to the banking market to support this approach, as part of its missions. Regarding the financing of investment, the sharp increase in the share of medium- and long-term loans in total credits, observed over the last ten (10) years (from 57% in 2009 to 75% in 2018) is mainly the result of that of long-term loans related to the financing of investments, in the energy and water sectors. Indeed, even if the financing of the economy has undeniably increased in recent years, as indicated by the annual increase in credit growth rates (8.7% in 2016, 12.3% in 2017 and 13.8% in 2018), the fact remains that this increase has not been fully inclusive of all sectors of the economy. As a reminder, loans to the economy reached 49.9% of GDP in 2018, (from 7.909 billion DA at the end of 2016, to 10.102 billion DA in 2018). As a result, in the future, financing should be more directed towards projects in manufacturing industries and productive services carried out by small and medium-sized enterprises, with proven added value. From this point of view, improving the capacity of banks and financial institutions to support the creation and development of productive SMEs is required, as well as boosting their customer advisory activities and in particular expertise in project analysis, which are professions that banks must necessarily develop to promote the development of investment loans and better manage risks. The Bank of Algeria devotes permanent efforts to the promotion of this segment of banking activity, in particular through the upgrading and modernization of its centrals (risk and non-payment management), at the service of the banking community. The improvement and development of bank intermediation should, necessary, be based on the modernisation of banks' information systems. These systems will make it possible to expand the range of products and services to customers as well as the reliable and exhaustive reporting of information, a necessary support for effective bank management and more efficient supervision by the Bank of Algeria, able to ensure sustainable financial stability, at the service of a diversified and dynamic economic activity. In this regard, the Banking Commission is preparing to request that banks and financial institutions conduct audits of their information systems, on the basis of exhaustive and standardized specifications. In line with developments around the world, the modernisation of our banks and financial institutions should resolutely turn to digitalisation, a powerful vector for greater financial inclusion, both in terms of collecting savings and facilitating access to credit. The Bank of Algeria devotes permanent efforts, including through policy notes and appropriate regulatory texts, to promote the achievement of these objectives, on the basis of the sustainable restoration of the necessary trust between the banking and financial centre and the clientele of savers and investors. As such, the permanent and high-level consultations, which have become customary between the heads of the Bank of Algeria and the banking and financial centre, are likely to promote a fruitful dialogue, with the aim of developing, in the well-understood interest of the place and its environment, the regulatory and operational frameworks, which must support the objectives assigned, among which the strengthening of the trust shared between the place and its customers. These various challenges seem to be within the reach of the banking and financial centre, whose resilience to external shocks has been tested for four (04) years, with a high potential for profitability and an adequate recapitalisation. "It is therefore up to this place to address banking and financial reform, which must aim at both diversification and dynamisation of the credit offer, without forgetting the strengthening of banks' capacities to drain more savings in the context of bank intermediation, which must be characterised by more assertive fair competition. To this end, banks are invited to work on a permanent upgrade of their human resources and their qualifications, with a view to approaching this financial reform with a stronger aptitude for new induced professions. These are, succinctly, my observations on the requirements and challenges that banks and financial institutions are called upon to meet, within the framework of the necessary effective modernization, for the accomplishment of their missions, as an engine of growth of the economy and its diversification. I thank you for your attention and wish you every success in your work.

Elle doit constituer le signal fort de lorientation des ncessaires rformes bancaires,  mme de promouvoir la concurrence et davantage defficacit dans lintermdiation bancaire. La collecte des ressources est lun des talons dAchille du systme bancaire algrien. De ce fait  lavenir, les financements devraient sorienter davantage vers les projets dans les industries manufacturires et les services productifs ports par les petites et moyennes entreprises,  valeur ajoute avre. La Banque dAlgrie consacre des efforts permanents pour la promotion de ce segment dactivit des banques, notamment  travers la mise  niveau et la modernisation de ses centrales ( gestion des risques et des impays), au service de la communaut bancaire. Lamlioration et le dveloppement de lintermdiation bancaire devrait, ncesssairement, reposer sur la modernisation des sytmes dinformation des banques. Ces systmes permettront aussi bien dlargir la gamme des produits et des services vers la clientle que la remonte fiable et exhaustive de linformation, support ncessaire pour une gestion efficace des banques et une supervision plus efficiente par la Banque dAlgrie,  mme dassurer une stabilit financire durable, au service dune activit conomique diversifie et dynamique. A cet gard, la Commission bancaire sapprte  demander la conduite, par les banques et tablissements financiers, daudits de leurs systmes dinformation, sur la base dun cahier des charges exhaustif et uniformis. En phase avec les dveloppements dans le monde, la modernisation de nos banques et tablissements financiers devrait se tourner rsolument vers la numrisation, vecteur puissant pour une plus large inclusion financire, tant en termes de collecte de lpargne quen termes de facilitation de laccs au crdit. La Banque dAlgrie consacre des efforts permanents, y compris  travers des notes dorientation et des textes rglementaires appropris, pour favoriser la ralisation de ces objectifs, sur la base du rtablissement durable de la ncessaire confiance entre la place bancaire et financire et la clientle dpargnants et dinvestisseurs. A ce titre, les consultations permanentes et de haut niveau, devenues coutumires entre les responsables de la Banque dAlgrie et de la place bancaire et financire, sont de nature  favoriser un dialogue fcond, aux fins de faire voluer, dans lintrt bien compris de la place et de son environnement, les cadres rglementaires et oprationnels, devant soutenir les objectifs assigns, parmi lesquels le renforcement de la confiance partage entre la place et sa clientle. Ces diffrents dfis semblent  la porte de la place bancaire et financire dont la rsilience aux chocs externes, a t prouve quatre (04) annes durant, avec un fort potentiel de rentabilit et une recapitalisation adquate.  Il appartient, ds lors  cette place, daborder la rforme bancaire et financire, devant viser  la fois une diversification et une dynamisation de loffre de crdit, sans oublier le renforcement des capacits des banques  drainer davantage lpargne dans le cadre dune intermdiation bancaire, devant tre caractrise par une concurrence loyale plus affirme. text: Presentation of the Governor of the Bank of Algeria Mr Rosthom Fadli International environment The year 2021, and despite the persistence of the COVID-19 pandemic, is marked by a gradual recovery in economic activity, global growth is projected at 5.88% at the end of 2021 against a contraction of 3.12% in 2020. The pandemic-induced economic crisis continues to put pressure on commodity prices. Indeed, between December 2019 and September 2021, the price indices for fuels, food products and raw materials of agricultural origin increased by 73%, 19% and 2% respectively. As for the minerals, ores and metals price index, it reached significant levels in the first half of 2021, but ended up falling in the third quarter, recording a decline of 0.3% between September 2021 and December 2020. It should be noted that the current levels of all the above-mentioned price indices are very high compared to pre-pandemic levels, indicating the continuing severity of this health and economic crisis, and its persistent effects on global inflation. At the level of the national real sector After recording a contraction during 2020, the recovery in national economic activity, which began in the first quarter of 2021 (2.3%), continued in the second quarter of 2021, reaching an appreciable growth of 6.4%, compared to a sharp contraction of 10.3% in the second quarter of 2020. This real GDP growth is correlated with higher growth in almost all major sectors of the national economy except "Agriculture", which fell slightly by 0.3% in the second quarter. 1 2021, compared to growth of 1.4% in the same period of the previous year. This decline is due in particular to unfavourable climatic conditions. Excluding hydrocarbons, GDP growth reached 6.1% in the second quarter of 2021 against a sharp decline of 11.5% in the second quarter of the previous year. The first sector that contributed to the growth of economic activity in the second quarter of 2021 was the "BTPH" sector, which recorded strong growth of 13.7% compared to -20.0% a year earlier. The second sector is "hydrocarbons", which grew by 11.0% compared to a decline of 5.3% in the second quarter of 2020. "Market services" posted growth of 10.2% compared to a sharp decline of 18.0% a year earlier. The "Industry" sector also achieved significant growth of 9.3% in the second quarter of 2021 compared to a decline of 5.3% in the second quarter of 2020. Balance of payments The evolution of the balance of payments is characterized by a sharp decline in the trade balance deficit of 8.933 billion in the first nine months of 2021, compared to the same period of 2020. Where the deficit increased from 10.504 billion at the end of September 2020 to 1.571 billion at the end of September 2021. This significant decline in the deficit is mainly due to the sharp increase in exports of goods, which rose from 16.240 billion at the end of September 2020 to 26.402 billion at the end of September 2021 (62.3%). In the first nine months of 2021, the average oil price rose 66.6%, from US41.365/barrel in the same period last year to US68.917/barrel. At the same time, the quantities of hydrocarbons exported, expressed in Tonnes of Oil Equivalent (TOE), increased by 20.9%. As a result, the total value of hydrocarbon exports rose sharply by 57.3%, from 14.868 billion at the end of September 2020 to 23.387 billion at the end of September 2021. Similarly, exports of non-hydrocarbon goods recorded a very significant increase, reaching 3.015 billion during the period under review compared to 1.372 billion at the end of September 2020. 2 (120 %). Imports of goods edged up 4.6% between September 2020 and September 2021, from 26.744 billion to 27.973 billion. Also, exports of services experienced relative stagnation at the end of September 2021, from 2.273 billion at the end of September 2020 to 2.300 billion at the end of September 2021, while imports of services, in the first nine months of 2021, recorded a decline of 630 million, from 5.644 billion at the end of September 2020 to 5.015 billion at the end of September 2021. In total, exports of goods and services reached 28.702 billion in the first nine months of 2021 compared to 18.513 billion in the same period of 2020, a sharp increase of 10.189 billion (55.04%). Imports of goods and services increased very slightly by 1.85%, from 32.388 billion at the end of September 2020 to 32.988 billion during the period under review. Thus, as a result of a sharp narrowing of the trade balance deficit and the significant decline in the item "services, excluding factor income" in the first nine months of 2021, the current account deficit fell sharply by 8.948 billion. From 14.491 billion at the end of September 2020 to 5.543 billion at the end of September 2021. The balance of the capital account and financial operations showed, at the end of September 2021, a surplus of 3.104 billion against 2.493 billion at the end of September 2020. That's up 611 million. These favourable developments led to a sharp contraction in the overall balance of payments deficit by nearly 10 billion in the first nine months of 2021, compared to the same period of 2020. Indeed, this deficit increased from 11.998 billion at the end of September 2020 to 2.439 billion at the end of September 2021. As a result, foreign exchange reserves, including SDRs and excluding gold, reached 44.724 billion at the end of September 2021. 3 Evolution of the dinar against the US Dollar and the Euro Developments in the algerian dinar remain strongly correlated with changes in economic fundamentals and fluctuations in the main reserve currencies on international foreign exchange markets. Thus, on average in the first eleven months of 2021, the Algerian dinar depreciated by 6.21% against the US dollar compared to the same period of the previous year when the recorded prices were 134.7387 USD/DZD in 2021 and 126.3681 USD/DZD in 2020. In terms of end-of-period variation, the Algerian dinar against the US dollar experienced a depreciation of 6.86% from USD 129.1328/DZD at the end of November 2020 to USD 138.6286/DZD at the end of November 2021, and a depreciation of 4.69% between the end of November 2021 and the end of 2020 where the recorded price was USD 132.1319/DZD. Against the euro, the Algerian dinar depreciated by 10.38% in terms of the average of the first eleven months of 2021 compared to the same period of the previous year when the recorded prices are 160.0275 EUR/DZD in 2021 and 143.4207 EUR/DZD in 2020. In terms of end-of-period variation, the Algerian dinar against the euro depreciated by 1.69% from EUR 154.3977 at the end of November 2020 to EUR/DZD 157.0593 at the end of November 2021, and an appreciation of 3.4% between the end of November 2021 and the end of 2020 when the price stood at EUR 162.4034/DZD. Monetary situation The M2 money supply recorded a growth of 12.79% during the first ten months of the current year, reaching 19,918.39 billion dinars against 17,659.64 billion dinars at the end of December 2020. This growth is mainly due to the increase in the M1 aggregate of 16.41%, from 11,901.82 billion dinars at the end of December 2020 to 13,854.50 billion dinars at the end of October 2021. Term deposits increased by 5.32%, reaching 6,063.89 billion dinars at the end of October 2021 against 5,757.82 billion dinars at the end of December 2020. The evolution of demand deposits, at the end of October 2021, was marked by a strong growth of around 23.54%, from 4,210.00 billion dinars at the end of 2020 to 5,201.23 billion dinars at the end of October 2021. The increase in demand deposits is mainly due to the growth in demand deposits of the national hydrocarbon company. 4 By legal sector, at the end of October 2021, public sector demand deposits increased by 46.20%. Similarly, demand deposits by private enterprises and households increased by 6.68% and 3.59% respectively. Recall that demand deposits represent at the end of October 2021, 26.1% of the money supply against 23.8% at the end of December 2020. As for term deposits, with a share of 30.4% in the money supply at the end of October 2021 against 32.6% at the end of December 2020, they reached 6,063.89 billion dinars, an increase of 5.32%. At the end of October 2021, public sector dinar term deposits decreased by 0.43%, in contrast to those of private companies and households, which recorded an increase of 3.84% and 6.75% respectively. As for foreign currency deposits, they grew by 9.74% reaching 927.21 billion dinars at the end of October 2021 Loans to the economy increased by 3.82% from 11,182.29 billion dinars at the end of December 2020 to 11,609.37 billion dinars at the end of October 2021. Thus, loans granted by public banks increased by 3.24% and those granted by private banks increased by 8.16% in the first ten months of 2021. Loans to public companies, private companies and households increased by 4.80%, 1.99% and 7.11% respectively at the end of October 2021. Bank liquidity Bank liquidity has contracted as a result of the economic repercussions of the health crisis. Nevertheless, in line with the monetary easing measures, the level of banks' overall liquidity improved significantly from October 2021 from 632.3 billion dinars at the end of December 2020 to 1,485.6 billion dinars at the end of November 2021. Thus, this increase is the direct result of the monetary policies decided by the Bank of Algeria in terms of lowering the reserve requirement rate. It should be recalled that this rate was reduced to 2% on 15 February 2021 after having lowered it from 10% to 8% on 15 March 2021, from 8% to 6% on 15 May 2020 and from 6% to 3% on 15 September 2020. Also, the Bank of Algeria has increased the refinancing thresholds for negotiable public securities, and extended the duration of the 5 refinancing from seven (7) days to one (1) month and to the full satisfaction of banks' refinancing requests. Finally, to support the economic recovery plan, the Bank of Algeria set up, on the first of July 2021, a special refinancing program, lasting one year, renewable twice, at the key rate and capped at 2,100 billion dinars. Evolution of inflation In October 2021, consumer prices in the city of Algiers increased by 1.3% compared to September 2021. This increase is mainly due to food prices, which rose by 2.3% in October 2021, and is supported by strong growth in the prices of fresh agricultural products, which increased by 4.1% in October 2021. Compared with the same month a year earlier, headline inflation accelerated by 5.96 percentage points year-on-year to 9.2% in October 2021. This evolution reflects the sharp increase in food prices, from 1.8% in October 2020 to 14.4% in October 2021, in line with the strong growth in the prices of fresh agricultural products, which recorded an increase of 16.5% in October 2021 against 1.9% in the same month of last year. Prices for manufactured goods remained up, reaching a rate of 6.2%, services prices rose by 2.3% in October 2021 compared to 0.7% in the same month of the previous year. Despite the major upheavals in the Algerian economy, it is important to note that monetary response policies have made it possible to mitigate to a very large extent the impact of the health crisis on both the real sector and the financial system in the context of a comfortable global external position. 6
