Title: Intervention to the National Popular Assembly on monetary and financial trends in 2015 and during the first nine months of 2016
text: BANK OF ALGERIA Monetary and financial trends in 2015 and the first nine months of 2016 and resilience and support in the context of a sustainable external shock Intervention of the Governor of the Bank of Algeria National People's Congress Monetary and financial trends in 2015 and the first nine months of 2016 and resilience and support policies in the context of a sustainable external shock In my presentation to your Honourable Assembly, I will endeavour to provide a global vision of the economic and financial situation of our country, in the context of the persistence of external shocks, analysed through highlights, in terms of economic activity, balance of payments, exchange rates, public finances, monetary developments and inflation, during the 2015 fiscal year and during the nine (09) months of 2016. Throughout my communication, I will provide guidance on the measures taken to address the persistent and severe impact of the oil counter-shock, in a context of market uncertainty, in order to preserve financial stability and support economic activity and its orientation towards greater diversification. Thus, monetary and financial developments, in 2015 and during the first three quarters of 2016, in our country, took place, in a context marked by the fragility of world economic activity, characterized by the weakness of the economic recovery, the continued slowdown in the growth of foreign trade, the fall in commodity prices - particularly drastic for oil prices and the acute nature of movements on the markets international exchange rates, mainly with a surge in the exchange rates of the US dollar against the euro. Given its heavy dependence on revenues from hydrocarbon exports, the national economy has been severely impacted by the fall in oil prices since June 2014, particularly on public finances, external accounts and bank liquidity. Fiscal and external current account deficits have widened considerably, leading to the almost total erosion of the resources of the revenue regulation fund and a significant decline in foreign exchange reserves. However, economic activity maintained its pace of the previous year, supported, mainly, by the maintenance of a high level of public spending. Although monetary expansion has been very subdued and monetary policy has remained cautious, inflation has resumed an upward trend, indicating the persistence of dysfunctions and distortions in some markets. In the monetary sphere, the oil shock marked a turning point in the evolution of certain aggregates compared to the long period 20012014, characterized by the gradual decrease in excess bank liquidity and, correspondingly, less recourse to its absorption by the Bank of Algeria. Financing of the economy, for its part, continued to expand at an appreciable pace; banking remained profitable and the banking system remained stable and resilient.  1  Finally, the flexibility of the dinar exchange rate, in the context of an external shock - and its impact on the fundamentals of the economy - and the sharp movements in the international exchange markets, has resulted in the depreciation of the national currency, particularly against the US dollar and, to a lesser extent, against the euro. The report of the Bank of Algeria that I had the honour to address to your Honourable Assembly, pursuant to Article 30 of the Law on Currency and Credit, analyses the main macroeconomic developments in 2015, highlighting in particular the impact of the sharp fall in oil prices on macroeconomic balances and economic policy measures, both cyclical and structural, to deal with it. 1. Economic activity. The large fiscal savings and the appreciable level of foreign exchange reserves accumulated in previous years have helped to contain the impact of the external shock on economic activity. As indicated in my introduction, economic growth has continued at a steady pace, stimulated, mainly, by the maintenance of public spending at a high level. Thus, during 2015, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 3.8%, the same pace as in 2014. This growth was driven by the agriculture, industry, BTPH and market services sectors. For its part, the hydrocarbon sector returned to positive growth of 0.4% for the first time since 2006, gaining one percentage point compared to the previous year (0.6%). Non-hydrocarbon GDP increased by 5.0%, marking a relative decline compared to 2014 (5.7%). At the end of the first half of 2016, GDP growth is estimated at 3.7%, with the continuation of the same trends as in 2015, i.e. growth in non-hydrocarbon sectors of 4.5% and growth in the hydrocarbon sector of 1.6%. The heavy dependence of economic activity on public spending is a major factor in the vulnerability of the national economy and raises the challenge of economic diversification, driven by a dynamic and competitive productive sector. The new model of economic growth, adopted by the Public Authorities, is part of this objective. The declination of its axes into concrete economic reforms and policies and their effective implementation could make it possible to anchor economic growth and employment in the long term. 2. Balance of payments. In 2015, the average price of a barrel of oil fell by 47.1%, from 100.2 in 2014 to 53.1 in 2015. This sharp fall in prices, combined with a slight decrease in the quantities of hydrocarbons exported, resulted in a decrease in revenues.  2  of hydrocarbon exports by 43.4% (33.08 billion in 2015 compared to 58.46 billion in 2014). With a slight decline in structurally weak non-hydrocarbon exports to 1.49 billion, total export receipts were 34.57 billion from 60.13 billion in 2014, down 42.5%. This drastic drop in total export revenues underlines the high vulnerability of external revenues to the volatility of oil prices, in a situation of structural weakness in non-hydrocarbon export earnings. This strongly militates in favour of sustained support for the export sectors. In this regard, the Bank of Algeria, for its part, introduced, during the 3rd quarter of 2016, two measures to relax exchange controls, namely: - 'Inward processing', which consists in abolishing the obligation on importers of inputs for the production of goods to be exported, to obtain an authorization from the Bank of Algeria for the settlement of the temporary import of these inputs and this, in the event that the payment of these imports is made by debiting their exporting currency accounts; - the extension of the periods for the repatriation of the proceeds of exports, which pass from 180 to 360 days, with the introduction of the obligation to take out export insurance when these periods exceed six (months). While preserving compliance with the obligation to repatriate, payments, this measure brings more flexibility to the exporter and allows him to obtain, from his bank, advances in dinars, backed by the insurance contract, to support his activity. At the same time, the Bank of Algeria is working to develop the interbank foreign exchange market, in particular by setting up its segment in the long term. This will provide the economic operator with the opportunity to hedge against currency risk and will help to strengthen the act of investing and exporting. Imports of goods, which have experienced an upward trend in recent years, fell in 2015, in a context marked by a sharp depreciation of the euro against the dollar (-16.55% on average per year). They stood at 52.65 billion in 2015, up from 59.67 billion in 2014, a decrease of 11.8%. This decline affected almost all groups of goods. The runaway imports of recent years has been contained thanks to measures including, mainly, the tightening of standards requirements, the preparation and implementation of the import control system, as well as measures taken by the Bank of Algeria. These include: - the strengthening of the requirements relating to the determination by banks of the financial area of the importer, for the needs of the bank domiciliation; - the reduction of the prudential ratio of banks' liabilities under the foreign trade, in relation to their own funds. This ratio has thus increased from two (2) times to one (1) times the bank's regulatory capital;  3  - the obligation of electronic pre-domiciliation, for the purposes of control a priority of the regularity of the operation with regard to the legislation and regulations in force; and - the intensification of controls on foreign trade operations directly at the level of bank branches. All these measures, in conjunction with those taken by the Public Authorities in this area, contribute to the rationalization of imports. However, it must be stressed that the problem of a viable level of imports, which contributes to the preservation of external balances without hindering economic growth, is closely linked to that of the development of local substitute production. As a result, the trade balance recorded a deficit of 18.08 billion in 2015, compared to a near equilibrium in 2014. As a result, and taking into account negative balances in services and factor income, the current account balance of payments recorded a record deficit of 27.48 billion in 2015 (16.5% of GDP), In total, the overall balance of payments recorded a deficit of 27.54 billion (compared to a deficit of 5.88 billion in 2014), with the capital account virtually balancing. As a result, the stock of foreign exchange reserves decreased by 34.81 billion (including the valuation effect), from 178.94 billion at the end of 2014 to 144.13 billion at the end of 2015. These trends continued in the first nine months of 2016 with: - a level of hydrocarbon export earnings of 19.40 billion, taking into account an average price per barrel of oil over the first nine months of the year, 42.69 and an export volume up 8.1%, compared to the first nine months of 2015; - a total revenue level of 20.38 billion; - a level of imports of 37.20 billion, down 2.99 billion dollars, compared to the level recorded, during the same period of 2015; - trade balance deficit of 16.82 billion, a deficit of current account of 22.24 billion and a balance of payments deficit of 21.42 billion; and  4  - a decrease in the stock of foreign exchange reserves, which fell by 144.1 billion of 121.9 billion at the end of September 2016. Given this level of official foreign exchange reserves, at the end of September 2016, still appreciable despite its sharp decline, and the very low level of external debt (3.09 billion, representing 1.87% of GDP in 2015), Algeria's external financial position remains relatively solid and comfortable. As an indication, official foreign exchange reserves, at the end of December 2016, amounted to 114.138 billion. For the whole of 2016, the decline in foreign exchange reserves amounted to 29.995 billion, including 25.609 billion in flows and 4.386 billion in negative valuation, due to the dollar translation effect of the share of reserves held in currencies other than the US currency. 3. Exchange Rate. The deterioration in the fundamentals of the economy  a fall in the price of oil, a high level of public spending and a widening of the inflation differential between Algeria and its main trading partners  in a context of sharp depreciation of the currencies of the main partner countries against the dollar, particularly in 2015, led to a depreciation of the nominal exchange rate of the dinar of about 20% against the US dollar and 3.8% against the euro in 2015. In the first half of 2016, the dinar depreciated by 2.94% against the US dollar and by 4.64% against the euro. It should be noted that in the face of falling oil revenues, the use of exchange rate flexibility is the first line of defence. Indeed, the flexibility of the dinar's exchange rate and the interventions of the Bank of Algeria on the interbank foreign exchange market have allowed the Dinar exchange rate to play, to a large extent, its role as a buffer of external shocks. As of the 3rd quarter of 2016, the exchange rate of the dinar against the US dollar has stabilized markedly, standing at: - 110.6 dinars for a dollar in May, - 110.4 dinars for a dollar in July, - 109.6 dinars for a dollar in August, - 110.4 dinars for a dollar in October, - 110.7 dinars for a dollar in August month of November and - 110.5 dinars for a dollar in December. Against the euro, the dinar experienced a relative appreciation, during the same period, its exchange rate rising from 125.6 dinars to the euro on May 3, 2016, to 120.23 in October and finally, to 117.6, at the end of November 2016 and to 116.4 on 15/12/2016.  5  The effective fiscal consolidation from 2017 onwards, as well as the prospects for stabilization or even a relative increase in oil prices, should contribute to a greater stability of the nominal exchange rate of the dinar. In the long term, the broadening and strengthening of fundamentals, through the diversification of the economy and the improvement of its competitiveness, as targeted in the framework of the new growth model, will be decisive to support a strong dinar. 4. Public Finance. Heavily dependent on oil taxation, public finances have been significantly impacted by the fall in oil prices. The corresponding decline in hydrocarbon tax revenues, but also the increase in public spending, resulted in the widening of the deficit in the overall balance of the treasury and the erosion of the resources of the Revenue Regulation Fund (FRR). Indeed, the revenues of the oil taxation of the year 2015, reached 2273.5 billion dinars against 3388.4 billion dinars during the year 2014. In the context of increased public spending, which rose from 6995.7 billion dinars in 2014 to 7656.3 billion dinars in 2015, an increase of 9.4%, the deficit of the overall balance of the Treasury reached 2621.7 billion dinars, or 15.8% of GDP, a historical record, against 8.0% in 2014. This deficit, financed, to the tune of 82.6%, from the resources of the Revenue Regulation Fund (FRR), led to a sharp decline in the outstanding amount of this Fund, which went from 4408.5 billion dinars at the end of 2014 to 2072 billion dinars at the end of 2015, an erosion of 53% in the space of a year. At the end of September 2016, public spending amounted to 5494.5 billion dinars, roughly the same level as in the first nine months of the previous year. During the same period, oil tax revenues continued to decline, reaching 1314 billion dinars, compared to 1934.1 billion dinars at the end of the first three quarters of 2015. The outstanding amount of the FRR, for its part, eroded further in early 2016, reaching the legal floor of 740 billion dinars from the end of February. The drastic reduction in budgetary savings and the prospects of long-term low oil prices call into question the need for fiscal consolidation in order to ensure the sustainability of public finances and restore internal balances in the long term. The Finance Act for 2017, in line with the envisaged medium-term fiscal consolidation framework, is rightly in line with this objective.  6  5. Monetary situation The consolidated monetary situation is characterised by a very weak expansion of the M2 money supply in 2015 (0.13%) and a very moderate growth of this aggregate, in the first nine months of 2016 (2.52%), in total contrast to the period 2010-2014, when the growth of the money supply (M2) averaged 13.8% per year. The analysis of the monetary situation highlights the following main developments, marked by the impact of the external shock: - a substantial decrease in demand deposits (excluding deposits with the CCP and the Treasury) in 2015 (-12.38%) and their very low growth over the first nine months of 2016 (0.16%). This reflects a very sharp contraction in hydrocarbon deposits (-41.09% and -14.24%, respectively) and a sharp slowdown in the growth of non-hydrocarbon deposits, i.e. 2.77% in 2015 and 3.14% in the first nine months of 2016, compared to 12.50% in 2014; - an increase in the relative share of non-bank fiat money in the money supply, which rose from 26.7% at the end of 2014 to 30% at the end of 2015 and 32.3% at the end of September 2016. The magnitude of this component of M2, which consists largely of the financial savings of hoarded households and fiat money in circulation in the informal sphere, militates for more efforts to collect resources by banks and sustained measures for the absorption of the informal economy. - a decrease in net foreign assets (consisting mainly of the stock of foreign exchange reserves expressed in dinars) of the order of 2.28% in 2015 and 12.94%, in the first nine months of 2016. The low level of this contraction, despite the sharp erosion of foreign exchange reserves, expressed in dollars (-57 billion dollars, between the end of December 2014 and the end of September 2016), is explained by the depreciation of the dinar against the US currency; - a deterioration in the Net Financial Position of the State vis-a-vis the banking system. Between the end of December 2014 and the end of September 2016, the State went from a position of net creditor (1992 billion dinars) to a position of net debtor vis-a-vis the banking system (- 2.024 billion dinars), under the effect of: the considerable use of the resources of the Revenue Regulation Fund (3668 billion dinars between the end of December 2014 and the end of September 2016);  7  the purchase by the Treasury of non-performing loans of public banks on public enterprises (305.3 billion dinars), by issuing securities, and the increase in bank loans to the State, mainly as a result of their subscriptions to the national loan (158.7 billion dinars); - the continued growth of credit to the economy, at an appreciable pace, despite unfavourable monetary and financial developments. Indeed, loans to the economy, before the Treasury buyback of non-performing loans held by public banks on public companies, increased by 16.57% in 2015 and by 14.87% in the first nine months of 2016. An analysis of the structure of credits to the economy reveals the following characteristics: o loans to large enterprises (mainly enterprises) public and mixed) represent 50.7% at the end of 2015 and 52.7% at the end of September 2016, against 49.3% and 47.3%, respectively, for loans to SMEs/ SMIs; o loans to large enterprises increased by 18.94% in 2015 and increased by a further 15.46% at the end of September 2016. For their part, loans to SMEs/SMIs (businesses and households) increased by 14.95% and 6.53%, respectively. Loans to households, mainly mortgages, increased by 15.13% in 2015 and by 10.67% in the first nine months of 2016; o by maturity, the distribution of credits to the economy remains relatively stable, with nearly 76% for medium- and long-term loans and nearly 24% for short-term loans; public banks account for 93.7% of total medium- and long-term loans distributed. This militates for more harmonious and solidarity involvement of the entire banking and financial system in the financing of productive investment; o the ratio of bank loans to deposits collected in dinars is from 74.7% at the end of 2014 to 83.7% at the end of 2015 and 92.5% at the end of September 2016; this indicates a decrease in the excess resources collected by banks compared to the loans distributed. Thus, banks' liquidity decreased, gradually, throughout 2015 and the first three quarters of 2016. It rose from 2731 billion dinars at the end of December 2014 to 1833 billion at the end of December 2015, to reach 992 billion at the end of September 2016, a decrease of 63.7% over the entire period, inducing a relative revival of activity on the interbank money market, hitherto sluggish.  8  Faced with this situation and in order to allow banks to have more loanable resources and to support the growth dynamic of loans to the economy, the Bank of Algeria first gradually reduced liquidity recoveries and completely interrupted them during the 3rd quarter of 2016. It also lowered the reserve requirement ratio from 12% to 8%. In addition, in anticipation of the further contraction of bank liquidity, in particular of public banks, the Currency and Credit Council approved, in July 2016, provisions supplementing those of Regulation No. 15-01 of 19 February 2015 on operations of discounting public bills, rediscounting of private bills, advances and credits to banks and financial institutions. These additional provisions allow the refinancing of certain segments of long-term loans - given the preponderance of their outstanding assets in banks' portfolios (more than 54% of loans) - as well as the partial refinancing of national debt bonds. At the same time, the rediscount rate was reduced from 4% to 3.5%, effective October 2, 2016. In addition, and to establish greater efficiency in the conduct of monetary policy and improve its transmission mechanisms, in this new context of liquidity need, which promises to be structural, the Bank of Algeria has specified, by means of instructions, dated 1 September 2016, the modalities of implementation of the instrument "open market operations" and the instrument "marginal lending facility". The first instrument allows the Bank of Algeria to manage its key interest rates and act on the liquidity of banks, according to the healthy financing needs of the economy and the inflation target. The second instrument, for its part, allows banks to cover their one-off cash flow needs with the Bank of Algeria. In order to contain the cost of bank financing of the economy, the Bank of Algeria has also fixed, by way of instruction promulgated on the same date, the maximum rate, called excessive rate, that banks and institutions can apply to their customers. Finally, it should be noted that, apart from the impact of the external shock on their liquidity, banks remain well capitalized, profitable and have only a small maturity asymmetry. However, the risks associated with the concentration of credit, mainly in public banks, engaged in the financing of major projects, remain significant. This requires rigorous monitoring, in order to avoid any threat to the stability of the financial system.  9  6. Inflation After the significant disinflation of 2013 and 2014, inflation rose again in 2015, reaching 4.8%, at an average annual rate. In September 2016, this rate reached 5.7%. The conduct of monetary policy, notably through the absorption of excess bank liquidity, has helped to contain more inflationary pressures, which could have resulted in a higher level of inflation. However, monetary policy action remains significantly hampered by dysfunctions and dominant positions in certain markets. This is corroborated by the fact that inflation, in 2015 and in the first nine months of 2016, is not of monetary origin; the money supply increased only very slightly. Nor can it be caused by inflation of import prices, in particular, in view of the low prices on international markets. Sustained efforts to remedy these situations of dysfunction and dominant positions would enable monetary policy to bring inflation under control more effectively, in line with its objective of price stability.  10  These are the main indicators that have characterized the macroeconomic environment, in the context of a severe and persistent external shock, it should be emphasized, the regulatory and structural measures intended to contain their harmful effects on the national economy as well as the forward-looking approaches recommended by the Public Authorities, with a view to stabilizing and consolidating the macroeconomic framework, with a view to greater diversification of the economy, a development of more banked savings and finally, the strengthening of our fundamentals.  11

Compte tenu de ce niveau des rserves officielles de change,  fin septembre 2016, encore apprciable en dpit de sa forte baisse, et du trs faible niveau de la dette extrieure (3,09 milliards de dollars, reprsentant 1,87 % du PIB de 2015), la position financire extrieure de lAlgrie demeure relativement solide et confortable. Taux de change. La dtrioration des fondamentaux de lconomie - chute du prix du ptrole, niveau lev des dpenses publiques et largissement du diffrentiel dinflation entre lAlgrie et ses principaux partenaires commerciaux , en contexte de forte dprciation des monnaies des principaux pays partenaires vis--vis du dollar, notamment en 2015, a entran une dprciation du taux de change nominal du dinar denviron 20 % par rapport au dollar amricain et de 3,8 % vis--vis de leuro en 2015. Il est  noter que face  la chute des recettes ptrolires, le recours  la flexibilit du taux de change, constitue la premire ligne de dfense. Finances Publiques. Fortement tributaires de la fiscalit ptrolire, les finances publiques ont t considrablement impactes par la chute des prix du ptrole. En contexte daccroissement des dpenses publiques, qui sont passes de 6995,7 milliards de dinars en 2014  7656,3 milliards de dinars en 2015, soit une hausse de 9,4 %, le dficit du solde global du Trsor a atteint 2621,7 milliards de dinars, soit 15,8 % du PIB, un record historique, contre 8,0 % en 2014. Ce dficit, financ,  hauteur de 82,6 %, par prlvement sur les ressources du Fonds de rgulation des recettes (FRR), a entran une forte baisse de lencours de ce Fonds, qui est pass de 4408,5 milliards de dinars  fin 2014  2072 milliards de dinars  fin 2015, soit une rosion de 53 % en lespace dune anne. A fin septembre 2016, les dpenses publiques se sont leves  5494,5 milliards de dinars, sensiblement le mme niveau que celui des neuf premiers mois de lanne prcdente. Au cours de la mme priode, les recettes de la fiscalit ptrolire ont poursuivi leur baisse, atteignant 1314 milliards de dinars, contre 1934,1 milliards de dinars au terme des trois premiers trimestres de 2015. Lencours du FRR, pour sa part, sest rod davantage en dbut de 2016, atteignant le plancher lgal de 740 milliards de dinars  compter de fin fvrier. Lamenuisement drastique de lpargne budgtaire et les perspectives de faiblesse durable des prix du ptrole, interpellent sur la ncessaire consolidation budgtaire, afin dassurer la viabilit des finances publiques et rtablir durablement les quilibres internes. La loi de Finances pour 2017, en phase avec le cadre de consolidation budgtaire  moyen terme envisag, sinscrit,  juste titre, dans cet objectif.  6  5. Situation montaire La situation montaire consolide se caractrise par une trs faible expansion de la masse montaire M2 en 2015 (0,13 %) et une croissance trs modre de cet agrgat, au cours des neuf premiers mois de 2016 (2,52 %), en contraste total avec la priode 2010-2014, o la croissance de la masse montaire (M2) a t de 13,8 % en moyenne annuelle. Lanalyse de la situation montaire fait ressortir les principales volutions suivantes, marques par limpact du choc externe : - une baisse substantielle des dpts  vue (hors dpts au CCP et au Trsor) en 2015 (-12,38 %) et leur trs faible croissance sur les neuf premiers mois de lanne 2016 (0,16 %). Cela reflte une trs forte contraction des dpts du secteur des hydrocarbures (-41,09 % et -14,24 %, respectivement) et un fort ralentissement de la croissance des dpts hors secteur des hydrocarbures, soit 2,77 % en 2015 et 3,14 % au cours des neuf premiers mois de 2016, contre 12,50 % en 2014 ; - une augmentation de la part relative de la monnaie fiduciaire hors banques dans la masse montaire, qui passe de 26,7 %  fin 2014  30 %  fin 2015 et  32,3 %  fin septembre 2016. Lampleur de cette composante de M2, constitue, en grande partie, de lpargne financire des mnages thsaurise et de la monnaie fiduciaire en circulation dans la sphre informelle, milite pour davantage defforts de collecte des ressources par les banques et des mesures soutenues pour la rsorption de lconomie informelle. - une diminution des avoirs extrieurs nets (constitus essentiellement du stock des rserves de change exprim en dinars) de lordre de 2,28 % en 2015 et de 12,94 %, au cours des neuf premiers mois de 2016. Le faible niveau de cette contraction, malgr la forte rosion des rserves de changes, exprimes en dollars (-57 milliards de dollars, entre fin dcembre 2014 et fin septembre 2016), sexplique par la dprciation du dinar vis--vis de la monnaie amricaine ; - une dtrioration de la position financire nette de lEtat  lgard du systme bancaire. Entre fin dcembre 2014 et fin septembre 2016, lEtat est pass dune position de crancier net (1992 milliards de dinars)  une position de dbiteur net vis--vis du systme bancaire (- 2,024 milliards de dinars), sous leffet :  du recours considrable aux ressources du Fonds de rgulation des recettes (3668 milliards de dinars entre fin dcembre 2014 et fin septembre 2016) ;  7   du rachat par le Trsor de crances non performantes des banques publiques sur des entreprises publiques (305,3 milliards de dinars), par mission de titres, et  de laugmentation des crdits des banques  lEtat, principalement suite  leurs souscriptions  lemprunt national (158,7 milliards de dinars) ; - la poursuite de la croissance des crdits  lconomie,  un rythme apprciable, malgr les dveloppements montaires et financiers dfavorables. En effet, les crdits  lconomie, avant rachat par le Trsor des crances non performantes dtenues par les banques publiques sur des entreprises publiques, ont progress de 16,57 % en 2015 et de 14,87 %, au cours des neuf premiers mois de 2016. Lanalyse de la structure des crdits  lconomie fait apparatre les caractristiques suivantes : o les crdits aux grandes entreprises (essentiellement les entreprises publiques et mixtes) reprsentent 50,7 %  fin 2015 et 52,7 %  fin septembre 2016, contre 49,3 % et 47,3 %, respectivement, pour les crdits aux PME/PMI ; o les crdits aux grandes entreprises ont connu une hausse de 18,94 % en 2015 et se sont encore accrus de 15,46 %  fin septembre 2016. De leur ct, les crdits aux PME/PMI (entreprises et mnages) se sont accrus de 14,95 % et 6,53 %, respectivement. Les crdits aux mnages, essentiellement des crdits hypothcaires, se sont accrus de 15,13 % en 2015 et de 10,67 % au cours des neufs premiers mois de 2016 ; o par maturit, la rpartition des crdits  lconomie demeure relativement stable, avec prs de 76 % pour les crdits  moyen et long terme et prs de 24 % pour les crdits  court terme ; les banques publiques comptant pour 93,7 % dans le total des crdits  moyen et long terme distribus. Cela milite pour davantage dimplication plus harmonieuse et solidaire de lensemble du systme bancaire et financier dans le financement de linvestissement productif ; o le ratio crdits bancaires par rapport aux dpts collects en dinars est pass de 74,7 %  fin 2014  83,7 %  fin 2015 et  92,5 %  fin septembre 2016 ; ce qui indique une baisse de lexcdent de ressources collectes par les banques comparativement aux crdits distribus. Ainsi, la liquidit des banques a diminu, progressivement, tout au long de lanne 2015 et des trois premiers trimestres de 2016. Elle est passe de 2731 milliards de dinars  fin dcembre 2014  1833 milliards  fin dcembre 2015, pour atteindre 992 milliards  fin septembre 2016, soit une baisse de 63,7 % sur lensemble de la priode, induisant un relatif regain dactivit sur le march montaire interbancaire, jusque-l, atone.  8  Face  cette situation et afin de permettre aux banques de disposer de plus de ressources prtables et daccompagner la dynamique de croissance des crdits  lconomie, la Banque dAlgrie a dabord rduit graduellement les reprises de liquidit et les a totalement interrompues, courant 3me trimestre 2016. Elle a galement baiss le taux de rserves obligatoires, qui est pass de 12 %  8 %. De plus, en prvision de la poursuite de la contraction de la liquidit bancaire, notamment des banques publiques, le Conseil de la monnaie et du crdit a approuv, au mois de juillet 2016, des dispositions compltant celles du rglement n 15-01 du 19 fvrier 2015 relatif aux oprations descompte deffets publics, de rescompte deffets privs, davances et crdits aux banques et tablissements financiers. Ces dispositions complmentaires autorisent le refinancement de certains segments des crdits  long terme - eu gard  la prpondrance de leur encours dans les portefeuilles des banques (plus de 54 % des crdits) - ainsi que le refinancement partiel des obligations de lemprunt national. Paralllement, le taux de rescompte a t ramen de 4 %  3,5 %,  compter du 2 octobre 2016. En outre, et pour asseoir une plus grande efficience dans la conduite de la politique montaire et amliorer ses mcanismes de transmission, dans ce nouveau contexte de besoin de liquidit, qui sannonce structurel, la Banque dAlgrie a prcis, par voie dinstructions, dates du 1er septembre 2016, les modalits de mise en uvre de linstrument  oprations dopen market  et de linstrument  facilit de prt marginal . Le premier instrument permet  la Banque dAlgrie de piloter ses taux dintrt directeurs et dagir sur la liquidit des banques, en fonction des besoins de financement sain de lconomie et de lobjectif dinflation. Le second instrument, pour sa part, permet aux banques de couvrir leurs besoins ponctuels de trsorerie, auprs de la Banque dAlgrie. Afin de contenir le cot de financement bancaire de lconomie, la Banque dAlgrie a galement fix, par voie dinstruction promulgue  la mme date, le taux maximum, appel taux excessif, que les banques et tablissements peuvent appliquer  leurs clientles. Enfin, il convient de signaler que, mis  part limpact du choc externe sur leur liquidit, les banques restent bien capitalises, rentables et ne prsentent quune faible asymtrie dchances. Cependant, les risques lis  la concentration du crdit, principalement dans les banques publiques, engages dans le financement de grands projets, demeurent importants. Cela appelle un suivi rigoureux, afin dviter toute menace sur la stabilit du systme financier.  9  6. Inflation Aprs la dsinflation significative des annes 2013 et 2014, linflation est repartie  la hausse en 2015, atteignant 4,8 %, en rythme annuel moyen. En septembre 2016, ce taux a atteint 5,7 %. La conduite de la politique montaire, notamment  travers labsorption de lexcs de liquidit bancaire, a permis de contenir davantage de pressions inflationnistes, qui auraient pu se traduire par un niveau dinflation plus lev. Cependant, laction de la politique montaire demeure contrarie, dans une importante mesure, par les dysfonctionnements et les positions dominantes sur certains marchs. Cela est corrobor par le fait que linflation, en 2015 et au cours des neufs premiers mois de 2016, nest pas dorigine montaire ; la masse montaire ne stant accrue que trs lgrement. Elle ne peut pas non plus tre cause par linflation des prix  limport, notamment, au vu de la faiblesse de ces prix sur les marchs internationaux. Des efforts soutenus pour remdier  ces situations de dysfonctionnements et de positions dominantes, permettraient  la politique montaire dassurer, de manire plus effective, la matrise de linflation, conformment  lobjectif de stabilit des prix qui lui est assign.  10  Telles sont les principaux indicateurs qui ont caractris lenvironnement macro-conomique, en contexte de choc externe, svre et persistant, faut-il le souligner, les mesures dordre rglementaire et structurel destines  contenir leurs effets dommageables sur lconomie nationale ainsi que les dmarches prospectives prconises par les Pouvoirs Publics , aux fins de stabiliser et consolider le cadre macro-conomique, dans la perspective dune plus grande diversification de lconomie, dun dveloppement dune pargne davantage bancarise et enfin, de renforcement de nos fondamentaux.  11

Title: Intervention on the role of central banks in promoting financial inclusion
text: BANK OF ALGERIA Role of central banks in promoting financial inclusion: reference to the case of Algeria Speech by Mohammed Laksaci Governor of the Bank of Algeria 21st Conference of Governors of Central Banks of French-speaking Countries (Dakar 14-15 May 2014) 1 Financial inclusion is becoming increasingly important in developing countries. By providing people without access to banking and financial services with the opportunity for minimum access to these services, it contributes to their integration into the economy, promote more inclusive growth and development, reduce poverty and strengthen social cohesion. In some developing countries, including Algeria, central banks pay particular attention to financial inclusion, complementing their traditional mandates of price stability and monetary and financial stability. In particular, the acuteness of financial exclusion in many African countries justifies the increased role of central banks in scaling up financial inclusion. Here I would like to outline recent developments in Algeria with regard to the financial inclusion framework, where the Bank of Algeria has been actively involved since 2010, and highlight the evolution of some indicators in this area. 1. To promote financial inclusion, a right to an account was introduced in 2010 by a provision in the new Banking Law. This is the possibility offered for any citizen who does not have a bank account to access a free current account. This system, which was implemented by the Bank of Algeria in 2012, also provides for a number of operations to be free of charge. The legal provision contained in the banking law of 2010 allowed the Bank of Algeria to make effective the possibility for any citizen to access basic banking services. These facilitations are in line with the FATF's flexibility measures to promote financial inclusion and take into account its recommendations on combating money laundering and terrorist financing. The action of the Bank of Algeria has also extended to the content of the account agreement, which must include a number of provisions to give the bank-customer relationship more transparency. In terms of access to credit, the Bank of Algeria instructed banks in January 2013 to ensure compliance with the deadlines for processing credit applications submitted by customers. These deadlines must not exceed fifteen (15) days for households and forty-five (45) days for small and medium-sized enterprises. Banks with large networks have also been asked to provide an information service at each counter for the benefit of customers, more particularly for the preparation of files accompanying the application for investment credits for the benefit of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This helps to facilitate access to credit, while taking into account potential risks to financial stability. With regard to consumer protection actions, the main legal provision adopted in 2010 is the obligation for banks to grant an eight-day withdrawal period to customers in order to be able to renege on their commitment to take out credit without having to suffer penalties. 2 More recently, the Finance Law for 2014 entrusted a new mission to the Bank of Algeria, that of promoting and regulating financial inclusion in its development dimension of the banking network throughout the national territory. The concept of financial inclusion adopted in this law, as set out in Article 35 bis, is broad. It goes beyond the sole perimeter of the difficulties of access and use relating to the bank account and the means of payment to integrate savings and credit. It aims to promote financial inclusion by encouraging the orderly intensification of the network of banks. In addition, and in order to ensure that access to banking services is as appropriate as possible, banks must ensure that the advertisements and materials they decline meet a number of standards, with the aim of informing customers as best as possible so that they can choose the products that best suit their needs. In this context, an instruction from the Bank of Algeria is being prepared and aims to charge banks a number of obligations, including: - the promotion of well-designed savings and credit products; - the opening of counters in rural areas and unfilled urban centres bank counters; - the obligation to respond to customer complaints. The establishment in 2006 by the Bank of Algeria and the banks of a modern, reliable and secure payments system has been a decisive support for the development of financial inclusion. The development of the payments system continues with the implementation by the Bank of Algeria, in 2014, of a new production platform and the update of payment software with regard to the RTGS. This modernisation also concerns the system of electronic tele-clearing of mass payments (small amounts) which will be accompanied by the development by banks of electronic payment instruments for individual use. The year 2014 will also see the modernization of the power plants and the implementation of a new system for sharing information on credits. All these developments will further facilitate the deepening of financial inclusion. 2. The efforts undertaken in recent years to boost financial inclusion have led to encouraging initial results, notably in 2013. Banks operating in Algeria, both public and private, are well capitalized and remain solid in view of the evolution of financial solidity indicators over the last four years. They are in excess of liquidity, characteristic of the money market for more than ten years. Public banks have developed their branch networks throughout the country, while the network of private banks is gradually developing. The situation in Algeria in terms of financial inclusion, as measured by indicators of the level of penetration, availability of banking services and use of these services, has evolved in recent years as follows: 3 - the level of penetration, expressed as the number of accounts opened in relation to the Total population, which remains the most relevant indicator, is increasing from 0.7 in 2010 to 0.8 in 2013. Compared to the population generally using deposit accounts (population aged 16 and over), the number of accounts per person was 1.15 in 2013 compared to 1.06 in 2011; - the number of bank counters (including SPC and Treasury counters) per population of 100,000 people is slightly increasing, i.e. 13.1 agencies in 2013 against 12.7 in 2010; - in the case of the use of banking services, the total deposits collected by the banks, CCPs and the Treasury relative to gross domestic product (GDP) has stabilized at around 59% over the past three years. The rate of deposits with banks, excluding deposits in the hydrocarbon sector, in relation to non-hydrocarbon GDP also remains relatively stable, at around 62% for the last three years. The credits distributed amounted to 44.2% of non-hydrocarbon GDP in 2013 against 40.6% in 2012 and 2011, knowing that the hydrocarbon sector does not use bank credits. Its capacity to self-finance its production and investment activities is such that it is in a position of net lender vis-a-vis the banking system. In terms of the distribution of micro-credits, the Algerian case is relatively different from the situations of financial inclusion, from the point of view of SMEs' access to credit, known by other countries on the continent. To enable young people to set up their small businesses, and thus promote the creation of youth employment, a national youth employment support agency (ANSEJ) was set up in 1996. The financing of the creation of this type of business is covered up to 70% by bank loans on favorable terms and for 30% by the endowment of the ANSEJ and the personal contribution of the future entrepreneur. At the end of 2013, through their support activity in this field, ANSEJ and the banks enabled the creation of more than 278,000 small businesses, contributing to a significant creation of jobs for young people. Another agency (Agence Nationale de Gestion du Micro Credit - ANGEM) was created in 2004 with the aim of contributing to the economic and social integration of targeted populations (housewives and citizens without income or with unstable and irregular income) by contributing to the creation of small jobs through the financing of raw materials and small equipment. The participation of public banks in the financing of young entrepreneurs through the ANSEJ scheme is appreciable. Out of a total financing of more than 825 billion dinars, loans granted by public banks amounted to more than 569 billion dinars at the end of 2013, contributing to the creation of more than 676,000 jobs. In particular, the level of distribution of micro-credits has increased over the last four years (2010-2013). This level represents 64% of the total micro-credits distributed by banks since the creation of the agency (569.4 billion dinars). 4 On the other hand, banks have participated little in the distribution of micro credits through ANGEM initiatives. This type of bank financing covers only 7% of the number of micro loans granted since 2005, when ANGEM began its activity. In total, significant efforts have been made in recent years in Algeria to promote inclusive economic activity, in particular by accelerating financial inclusion efforts, with the Bank of Algeria playing a significant role. Despite the progress made, much remains to be done to deepen financial inclusion over the medium term. These include: - accelerate banking, supported by the continued modernisation of the mass payments system in 2014 and an orderly densification of bank networks on the national territory; - to encourage the development of SME lending activity at bank level. The increased importance of bank loanable funds, which increasingly rely on the financial savings of private households and companies, offers a significant opportunity for a wider dissemination of healthy credit that can deepen financial inclusion. The completion of the modernization of the plants in 2014 will contribute to better management of the risks associated with such a release of credits; - further develop supervision from a risk perspective in order to preserve the financial stability. 5
text_original: BANK OF ALGERIA Rle des banques centrales dans la promotion de linclusion financire : rfrence au cas de lAlgrie Intervention de Mohammed Laksaci Gouverneur de la Banque dAlgrie 21e Confrence des Gouverneurs des Banques Centrales des Pays Francophones (Dakar 14-15 mai 2014) 1 Linclusion financire prend une importance accrue dans les pays en dveloppement. Dans certains pays en dveloppement, dont lAlgrie, les banques centrales accordent  linclusion financire une attention particulire, en complment de leurs mandats traditionnels de stabilit des prix et de stabilit montaire et financire. En particulier, lacuit de lexclusion financire dans beaucoup de pays africains justifie le rle accru des banques centrales dans lintensification de linclusion financire. Je voudrais ici esquisser les dveloppements rcents en Algrie en ce qui concerne le cadre de linclusion financire, o la Banque dAlgrie prend une part active depuis lanne 2010, et souligner lvolution de quelques indicateurs en la matire. 1. Pour promouvoir linclusion financire, un droit au compte a t instaur en 2010 par une disposition insre dans la nouvelle loi bancaire. Les efforts entrepris au cours des rcentes annes en matire dimpulsion de linclusion financire ont permis dobtenir de premiers rsultats encourageants, notamment en 2013. Title: Development of alternative finance in Algeria - parliamentary day
text: Development of alternative finance in Algeria Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Algeria Parliamentary Day  03 April 2018 First of all, I would like to welcome this commendable initiative by your honourable institution. The organization of this parliamentary day reflects, in fact, the growing importance within Algerian society of the introduction or development of banking and financial products compatible with the precepts of Sharia law. These instruments will undoubtedly contribute to the enrichment of the range of banking and financial products likely to capture the large share of the money in circulation outside the banking circuit and to direct it towards productive jobs, thus promoting more performance in terms of banking and financial intermediation, while meeting a legitimate expectation of savers. Experience around the world in the use of these instruments has been greatly enriched in recent years and can constitute an appreciable fund from which banks and financial institutions in Algeria can validly draw. This will allow the Algerian banking and financial system to move more quickly in this direction, especially since this segment has experienced only a weak development since its introduction in Algeria, with the establishment of two specialized institutions and this, despite signals of strong enthusiasm in this area. Indeed, alternative finance is struggling to assert itself on the ground in Algeria, where it constitutes only a very small share of the global banking and financial market. Public banks, hitherto almost absent from this segment, and given their preponderant weight in the banking and financial sector, i.e. 87% of market share, can be a decisive vehicle for the generalization of these products, ensuring them an exhaustive geographical coverage through their wide establishment in terms of networks. This would be in line with the dual desire, displayed by both the public authorities and the public banks themselves, to promote and popularize these instruments of alternative finance, for the benefit of greater financial inclusion. At the same time, this should contribute, as already pointed out, to draining a significant part of the money supply in circulation outside banks or hoarded, towards the 1 financing productive employment, and supporting ongoing efforts to address financing difficulties through conventional channels. The development of these instruments must be based on the establishment, at the level of the banks and financial institutions concerned, of separate and adequate information, accounting and management systems, as well as appropriate procedural arrangements and reserved areas. Banks and financial institutions must also have qualified staff exclusively dedicated to this segment of finance. This is a major requirement for banks, especially public ones, which decide to open specific windows to alternative instruments. The distinction and impermeability between the two categories of activities must be scrupulously observed. In accordance with the legislative and regulatory provisions, the effective launch of these products on the market by banks and institutions must have obtained, beforehand, the notice of no objection from the Bank of Algeria. Indeed, in accordance with the missions assigned to it by law, the Bank of Algeria, while encouraging the enrichment of the range of banking products of the place, ensures the stability and security of the banking system as a whole. As such, it ensures that the risks associated with the intermediation activity of any bank and financial institution, whatever the nature of the products concerned, are effectively identified and contained and are not likely to weaken the system as a whole. It also ensures that the customers of banks and institutions are protected from excessive practices. To date, the Bank of Algeria has been the recipient of requests for notices of no objection, from three (03) public banks and one private bank, relating to alternative products. These applications are ongoing. For some products, deficiencies in terms of maturation have been identified and communicated to the banks concerned for adaptation. In addition, the Bank of Algeria will ensure the effective implementation of the requirements and prerequisites for the exploitation of these products, as already mentioned. A regulation in preparation, which will soon be submitted to the Mint and Credit Council for review and approval, will further clarify these requirements in organizational, procedural and accounting matters, as well as in terms of staff training and qualification. Finally, it should be noted that the Bank of Algeria provides an opinion of no objection on the nature of a banking product authorized to be marketed. The Bank of Algeria does not provide a notice of compliance of these products with the precepts of Sharia. This falls within the competence of the religious authorities, who are the only ones empowered to issue this opinion. 2 It will therefore be up to the banks and financial institutions, after obtaining the notice of no objection from the Bank of Algeria, to collect this notice of compliance from these authorities. Finally, I would like to stress once again that the Bank of Algeria encourages this orientation in terms of broadening the range of banking and financial products, in particular because they are likely to contribute to a greater mobilization of the money supply in circulation excluding Banks, while meeting the expectations expressed by some of the potential customers. 3

Title: Statement to the International Monetary and Financial Committee
text: BANK OF ALGERIA Statement by Mr Mohammed Laksaci Governor of the Bank of Algeria to the Monetary Committee and Financier International On behalf of Afghanistan, Algeria, Ghana, islamic republic of Iran, Morocco, Pakistan and Tunisia Saturday, April 18, 2015 I take this opportunity to express our appreciation to Mr Tharman for the quality of his chairmanship of the IMFC and to extend a warm welcome to his successor, Mr Agustin Cartsens, who is well known to all of us. We look forward to working together, under his presidency, to meet the expectations of the members of our institution in these difficult times. In an increasingly volatile environment, the recovery of the global economy has continued, albeit at a moderate and uneven pace, reflecting a slight recovery in growth in advanced economies and a slower but still solid pace of growth in emerging and developing economies. The drastic fall in oil prices and, to a lesser extent, the fall in the prices of other commodities, have had a significant impact on the world economy, with differentiated effects on oil-exporting and oil-importing countries. While growth is expected to strengthen in 2015, the recovery remains too frail to put the global economy on a solid path and reduce unemployment. Risks are more balanced than in the past, but significant downside risks remain. The IMF's work on potential growth raises concerns about medium-term growth prospects in all countries, and we look forward to refinement of the analysis, including a more elaborate assessment of the impact of recent structural reforms. In the United States, the pace of growth continues to strengthen and has translated into sustained job creation, while in the euro area, welcome signs of an early recovery are emerging, supported by lower oil prices and the depreciation of the euro. Although fragilities in this area remain, including in relation to very low inflation, the recent launch of asset purchases by the ECB augurs well for prospects for recovery and mitigation of deflation risks. In emerging markets, growth continues to decelerate after peaks in previous years, with country-specific variations reflecting specific circumstances and geopolitical factors. Nevertheless, emerging market and developing economies continue to account for most of global growth. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region continues to face unprecedented challenges arising from regional conflicts and security considerations. Although the fall in oil prices 2 has a positive impact on oil-importing countries, most exporting countries are led to use their savings to soften the negative impact of this decline on public spending and growth. Despite these challenges, it is somewhat comforting that overall growth in the region is projected at 3% in 2015 and 3.7% in 2016. Given the many challenges facing the global economy, we support the Director-General's Global Policy Agenda, which highlights goals and policies to support growth and jobs, strengthen financial stability and resilience to shocks, promote inclusion and equal opportunities. economic, including for women. The primary responsibility for designing and implementing appropriate policies to address country-specific challenges rests with each of these countries, but in view of the integration of the global economy, it is necessary to take into account cross-border spillovers in domestic policies. We therefore attach great importance to the IMF's coordinating role and surveillance mission at both the bilateral and multilateral levels. Supporting domestic demand remains crucial in advanced economies to strengthen the recovery. This requires the continuation of accommodative monetary policies, the strengthening of monetary policy transmission mechanisms, and appropriate communication on monetary policy announcements in order to mitigate the effects of potentially destabilizing spillovers. Fiscal policies must also be more supportive of growth and jobs, taking into account the availability of fiscal capacity and progress in public debt sustainability. Addressing the legacy of the crisis in the financial sector, particularly in the euro area, will help improve the functioning of credit markets and stimulate private sector demand and economic activity. Emerging and developing economies also face many challenges, including strengthening the resilience of their economies to shocks emanating from monetary policy normalization in advanced economies, including tightening financing conditions, increased volatility in capital flows, and abrupt exchange rate movements. The policy mix will require a calibration between supporting growth, containing inflation, accumulating fiscal and external buffers, strengthening financial stability and internal capital markets. Strengthening the fiscal framework and improving the investment climate are key to improving investor confidence. Although they continue to record robust growth, low-income developing countries are not immune to spillovers from low growth in advanced and emerging economies as well as commodity price volatility.3 In addition, these countries continue to face challenges related to the reduction of high poverty, job creation and the improvement of social indicators. This highlights the importance of pro-growth fiscal policies, focused on strengthening income mobilization, improving the structure of public spending to promote infrastructure investment and pro-poor spending, reforming energy subsidies, and rationalizing current spending. These policies, however, will not generate the expected results without appropriate external financial support and we look forward to the IMF's contribution to the upcoming conferences on financing for development and climate change. We welcome the establishment of the Disaster Containment and Relief Trust, which has already been used to support countries affected by the Ebola outbreak, and call on the international community to adequately fund this fund. We also call for flexible implementation of the debt limit policy to help member countries complement external concessional financial resources with market-based financing to meet their infrastructure and other development needs, while preserving external debt sustainability. The World Economic Outlook provides a comprehensive assessment of the impact of low oil prices on the global economy as well as on the economies of specific groups of countries. We welcome the work and broadly endorse the differentiated advice addressed to oil-producing and oil-importing countries. to cope with the effects of this fall in prices. We encourage the IMF to undertake more analytical work in this area to enhance the relevance of advice. IMF technical assistance would be useful in reforming subsidies and strengthening fiscal frameworks to protect fiscal policy from oil price fluctuations. We reiterate our call for the ratification and entry into force of the 2010 IMF governance and quota reforms, as well as our call for accelerated action towards agreement on a revised quota formula and the fifteenth General Review of Quotas. In the meantime, we call on the IMF Executive Board to continue to seek an interim solution that would significantly converge members' quotas to the levels agreed in the Fourteenth Review.
